title: ThirdKeyAI/Symbiont: v1.11.0 — symbi shell (Beta), /deploy stack, init Docker ergonomics, approval relay, cross-instance messaging
abstract: Added MCP-backed tool execution (mcp-client feature). ToolClad .clad.toml manifests can route a tool to an upstream Model Context Protocol server over stdio via an [mcp] block (server/tool/field_map), with servers declared in mcp-config.toml (per-project, then ~/.symbiont/). This replaces the previous placeholder in symbi run and the DSL reason()/tool_call() builtins with real execution; when no tools/ manifests are present those paths now return an honest "no tool backend" error instead of a fabricated success. Invocation is SchemaPin-verified fail-closed by default (TOFU key pinning; a post-pin key swap at the provider key URL is rejected as KeyMismatch), with ToolCladExecutor::with_mcp_verification(false) as a local-dev opt-out. The default build does not pull the MCP client transport. See docs/mcp-tools.md. Live RAG retrieval in interactive chat. The WebSocket coordinator now wires a real KnowledgeBridge (over StandardContextManager + LanceDB) into the reasoning loop, so knowledge retrieval and the recall_knowledge / store_knowledge tools run for live agents. RAG turns on when built with the vector-lancedb feature and an embedding provider is configured (EMBEDDING_* / OPENAI_API_KEY); otherwise it stays off with a clear log. The previously-silent mock-embedding fallback now warns loudly, and SYMBIONT_REQUIRE_REAL_EMBEDDINGS=1 makes an unconfigured provider fail fast. Reasoning-loop robustness (issue #20). The ORGA loop now fails over on model refusal and no-progress turns instead of stalling; Anthropic requests support prompt caching and extra-parameter passthrough; the output-token cap is configurable; and 1M-context models report the correct context-window size. Fixed Browser tools no longer fabricate success. mode = "browser" ToolClad tools were wired live but had no CDP backend, so every command returned a fake "status":"success" envelope. They now run argument validation and the scope deny-by-default guard, then return an honest error (gated behind the new toolclad-browser feature) until a real Chrome DevTools Protocol backend is added. No build enables browser execution by default. MCP tool arguments keep their declared JSON types. A manifest arg typed integer/number/boolean/array/object is sent to the upstream MCP server as the matching JSON type instead of an always-quoted string. MCP tool calls are time-bounded. A per-call timeout (the tool's timeout_seconds, capped by the loop's tool_timeout) prevents a hung or slow MCP server from hanging the caller, including the DSL tool_call() path. Anthropic refusals are surfaced. A model refusal now maps to FinishReason::Refusal (with a warning on no-progress turns) instead of silently no-op'ing tool-driven agents. Backend-less runners are honest. symbi run and the DSL reasoning builtins return a clear "no tool backend" error rather than a fabricated success when no tools are configured. Security opentelemetry_sdk 0.31 → 0.32 — clears GHSA-w9wp-h8wv-79jx (W3C Baggage unbounded allocation). serde_with → 3.21.0 — clears GHSA-7gcf-g7xr-8hxj (KeyValueMap serialization panic on empty sequence/map entries). dompurify → 3.4.12 (symbi-a2ui) — clears GHSA-c2j3-45gr-mqc4 (CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING sanitizer bypass). crossbeam-epoch → 0.9.20 — clears RUSTSEC-2026-0204 (invalid pointer dereference in the fmt::Pointer impl for Atomic/Shared); spin bumped to 0.9.9 to drop the yanked 0.9.8. Changed ethnum → 1.5.3 — 1.5.2 no longer compiles on current stable Rust.

title: Causal Learning for Continuous Variables with an Improved Bayesian Network Constructed by Symmetric Kernel Function Acceleration
abstract: Bayesian network-based causal structure learning provides an effective framework for uncovering causal relationships among continuous variables. However, many existing methods for continuous data still rely on strong parametric distribution assumptions, which may introduce information loss and reduce Bayesian network modeling accuracy. Kernel density estimation (KDE), a non-parametric statistical method that is more flexible in density estimation form, offers a versatile framework for conducting conditional independence (CI) tests. This approach enables the estimation of mutual information and conditional mutual information, thereby facilitating the identification of underlying structural relationships. Nevertheless, the high computational cost of KDE-based CI testing restricts its practical application in continuous-variable causal learning. To address this issue, this study introduces a radial symmetric kernel-based acceleration scheme within a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) framework to improve the efficiency of density estimation. On this basis, an enhanced Bayesian network structure learning method is developed for continuous variables, enabling more efficient estimation of mutual information and conditional mutual information while improving the computational efficiency and empirical stability of variable dependency discovery. With proper bandwidth and grid resolution, the proposed MMHC-FFTKDE framework achieves a reduction in computational runtime and improves efficiency compared to MMHC-KDE in the ablation setting, while maintaining competitive F1-scores and SHD for causal structure discovery.

title: Integrating Mental Health and Juvenile Justice Outcomes: A Case Study of Model-Agnostic Interpretable Machine Learning
abstract: When the justice system places juveniles into correctional institutions and recidivism rates rise, society bears substantially higher costs compared with when juveniles are placed at home or in community-based alternatives. Research indicates that mental health conditions, rather than public safety concerns, drive decisions to send juveniles to institutions. However, juvenile justice and mental health data are rarely combined for analysis, depriving policymakers of crucial insights to improve juvenile justice outcomes. Identifying the predictive factors of institutional placement is crucial to developing targeted early interventions. We introduce marginal contribution weighting (MCW), a method that compares feature importance across predictive models using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) values to inform policy decisions. MCW preserves Shapley properties and maintains factorial weighting for marginal contributions, allowing a fair comparison of feature contributions. We apply MCW to a case study in the U.S. state of Texas that integrates mental health and juvenile justice data to predict court-ordered out-of-home placements. We develop a machine learning model using juvenile justice data and then incorporate mental health treatment records to evaluate the impact of new mental health features on accuracy and explainability. By systematically quantifying the impact of mental health features using MCW and SHAP-based analysis, our approach provides a rigorous framework for assessing feature importance across models. This methodology highlights the predictive value of mental health treatment data and ensures fairness in feature comparisons. By identifying key risk factors, our approach provides justice, law enforcement, and correctional policymakers with data-driven insights to support preventive, community-based strategies and mitigate the adverse effects of institutionalization on youth development and long-term outcomes. History: This paper has been accepted by Kaushik Dutta for the Special Issue on Responsible AI and Data Science for Social Good. Supplemental Material: The software that supports the findings of this study is available within the paper and its Supplemental Information ( https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/suppl/10.1287/ijoc.2024.0663 ) as well as from the IJOC GitHub software repository ( https://github.com/INFORMSJoC/2024.0663 ). The complete IJOC Software and Data Repository is available at https://informsjoc.github.io/ .

title: Application of Item Response Theory in English Teaching System Design: An Adaptive Learning Framework Based on Neural IRT and CAT
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework integrating Neural Item Response Theory (Neural IRT) with Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT) for designing personalized English teaching systems. Traditional English instruction often suffers from fixed difficulty levels and limited personalization, leading to suboptimal learning outcomes. By modeling student ability across three core dimensions—vocabulary, grammar, and reading—we employ a 2PL-based Neural IRT model enhanced with light L2 regularization to dynamically estimate latent traits and item parameters. The system implements Fisher information-based adaptive item selection, enabling real-time tailoring of exercises to individual proficiency levels. Extensive simulations on a dataset of 500 students and 120 items demonstrate superior performance in parameter recovery, testing efficiency, and learning gains compared to fixed-item and random baselines. The proposed approach not only improves assessment accuracy but also fosters balanced skill development in English learning. Key contributions include the integration of multi-dimensional IRT with adaptive recommendation, detailed empirical validation through composite visualizations, and practical implications for AI-driven language education platforms. This work advances the application of psychometrics in intelligent tutoring systems, offering a scalable solution for modern English pedagogy.

title: Multilingual Converged Media Data Processing for Brand Influence Evaluation of Multinational Enterprises
abstract: Against the backdrop of deep integration of globalization and converged media, the evaluation of enterprise brand influence urgently needs to break through the limitations of single-language and traditional data processing methods. This paper takes large energy-based multinational enterprises (MNEs) as the research object, and focuses on the application path of multilingual converged media data processing technology in brand evaluation by combining global brand influence evaluation theories and practices. A multilingual data processing framework adapted to enterprise brand evaluation is established via constructing a multilingual corpus collection system, optimizing the Domain Adaptation-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory-Conditional Random Field (DA-BiLSTM-CRF) cross-lingual word segmentation algorithm and the "adversarial transfer + bilinear attention" sentiment analysis algorithm. This framework solves the problems of narrow data coverage, low accuracy of sentiment analysis, and poor cross-lingual adaptability in traditional evaluations. Research shows that the DA-BiLSTM-CRF cross-lingual word segmentation model and the improved cross-lingual sentiment classification method can effectively improve the accuracy and efficiency of multilingual brand data processing, providing more comprehensive and reliable data support for brand influence evaluation. It is particularly suitable for brand evaluation practices of large MNEs with global business layouts.

title: An Intelligent System for Automated Document Generation
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent document generation system that automatically creates professional documents using natural language processing and machine learning techniques. The proposed system combines template-based document structure with transformer-based content generation to produce clear, well-organized, and context-aware documents. The architecture includes an input analysis module to understand user requirements, an adaptive template selection module to choose the appropriate document format, a neural content generation component to generate meaningful text, and a quality validation module to check accuracy and consistency. The system also uses adaptive learning to improve document quality based on user feedback. Experimental results show a document structure accuracy of 92.3 percent and a content relevance score of 89.7 percent, while reducing document creation time by about 75 percent compared to manual writing. The system was tested on technical, academic, business, and legal documents. A user study with 150 participants achieved an average satisfaction score of 4.3 out of 5, demonstrating that the system is effective, easy to use, and suitable for real-world document generation applications

title: Qubit-Scalable CVRP via Lagrangian Knapsack Decomposition and Noise-Aware Quantum Execution
abstract: Hybrid quantum optimization for vehicle routing faces a practical bottleneck: direct QUBO encodings of CVRP quickly exceed near-term qubit and gate budgets, while quantum evaluations are expensive, noise-limited, and sensitive to backend and circuit configuration. We address this gap with an end-to-end decomposition pipeline that converts CVRP into bounded-width quantum subproblems and treats quantum execution as a decision problem within the optimization loop. Starting from a Fisher--Jaikumar assignment linearization, we apply Lagrangian relaxation to dualize customer-assignment couplers, yielding independent per-vehicle knapsack subproblems that admit QUBO/Ising evaluation. To replace brittle subgradient tuning, we learn a multiplier-update controller using expert-guided pretraining followed by reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, with rewards based on execution-realized progress and route reconstruction. We also introduce a constrained contextual bandit as a hardware-aware execution layer that selects backend and circuit configuration with feasibility screening, enabling adaptation across heterogeneous noisy resources and parallel multi-QPU scheduling. Computational results on multiple CVRPLIB families show that the decomposition yields stable bounded-width subproblems across instance sizes, learned multiplier updates improve end-to-end routing quality relative to classical subgradient control under matched budgets, and hardware-mode configuration reduces median optimality gaps relative to static execution choices in our test set. We do not claim quantum advantage. Instead, the contribution is a practical end-to-end framework for scaling hybrid quantum CVRP optimization through OR decomposition, learning-augmented dual control, and adaptive hardware-aware execution.

title: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Comparing Voice and Text Explainability
abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) aims to make machine learning models transparent and trustworthy, yet most current approaches communicate explanations visually or through text. This paper introduces an information-theoretic framework for analyzing how explanation modality—specifically, voice versus text—affects user comprehension and trust calibration in AI systems. The proposed model treats explanation delivery as a communication channel between model and user, characterized by metrics for information retention, comprehension efficiency (CE), and trust calibration error (TCE). A simulation framework implemented in Python was developed to evaluate these metrics using synthetic SHAP-based feature attributions across multiple modality–style configurations (brief, detailed, and analogy-based). Results demonstrate that text explanations achieve higher comprehension efficiency, while voice explanations yield improved trust calibration, with analogy-based delivery achieving the best overall trade-off. This framework provides a reproducible foundation for designing and benchmarking multimodal explainability systems and can be extended to empirical studies using real SHAP or LIME outputs on open datasets such as the UCI Credit Approval or Kaggle Financial Transactions datasets.

title: Claude Code's Hidden Context Tax
abstract: Episode summary: Bigger context windows don't mean unlimited working memory—Claude's hidden overhead can quietly degrade performance. This episode breaks down the hierarchy of context costs, from subagents (400-800 tokens each) to lazy-loaded MCP tools (near-free). Learn why eager vs. lazy loading matters more than raw size, how plugin sprawl inflates your startup tax, and practical optimizations to reclaim 25-30% of your effective context. The difference isn't just speed—it's the gap between a focused assistant and one that forgets mid-task. Show Notes ### The Hidden Costs of Claude's Context While Claude's expanded context window suggests limitless working memory, the reality is more nuanced. Not all primitives consume resources equally—some are "context vampires," silently draining capacity before you even begin a task. Understanding this hierarchy is key to maintaining performance. #### The Hierarchy of Context Hogs The heaviest costs come from **eager-loaded primitives**: - **Subagents** (400-800 tokens each): Their detailed example blocks are inlined verbatim, making them the most expensive. - **CLAUDE.md files**: Eager-loaded documentation that accumulates from root to working directory. - **Auto-memory**: Claude's self-written MEMORY.md can bloat to 25KB per session, crowding out active tasks. In contrast, **lazy-loaded tools** like MCPs (40-80 chars per name) and hooks (zero cost) are lightweight—but only if defaults like `ToolSearch` remain enabled. #### The Eager vs. Lazy Divide Cost isn't about size alone—it's about **when** a primitive loads. A 200-line skill invoked on demand is cheaper than a 10-line subagent description loaded upfront. Key takeaways: - **Disable unused plugins**: Even inactive plugins may inject eager-loaded agents via `settings.json`. - **Audit subagents**: Replace verbose examples with shorter ones, or convert them to skills. - **Scope CLAUDE.md**: Split monolithic files into path-specific rules. #### The Plugin Pitfall Installing a plugin often means adopting its hidden eager loads—like main-thread agent swaps that replace Claude's core prompt silently. The fix? Regularly audit plugins with `/plugin` and grep for `"agent"` keys. **Optimization Payoff** A few tweaks—disabling auto-memory, trimming subagents, and scoping documentation—can reclaim 25-30% of working context. The result? Faster, more reliable responses without mid-task amnesia. Listen online: https://myweirdprompts.com/episode/claude-code-context-bloat

title: USING MODERN DRONE TECHNOLOGY IN THE MINING OF RARE EARTH ORES
abstract: The application of modern drone technologies in the mining of rare earth metals (REEM) ores is revolutionizing the mining industry. This article examines the application of drones in the exploration, mapping and mining of REEM ores. Drones equipped with hyperspectral cameras, LiDAR sensors and magnetometers provide faster, safer and more cost-effective results compared to traditional methods. Results and discussions are presented based on a literature review and methodology. As a result, proposals are made to optimize the extraction of REEM ores using drone technologies and reduce environmental impact.

title: AI-Driven Personalized Pathways for Real Estate Law Education via Continual Knowledge Graphs and Reinforcement Optimization
abstract: This Paper propose Adaptive Legal Learning (ALL), a novel AI-driven framework for personalized real estate law education that dynamically adapts to both learner competencies and evolving legal knowledge. Traditional competency-based systems often fail to account for rapid regulatory changes and case law updates, hence This Paper introduce a Continual Legal Knowledge Graph (CLKG) that incrementally integrates new legal concepts and relationships through a fine-tuned Legal-BERT model and a graph neural network-based relational inferencer. The framework further employs a Reinforcement-Based Pathway Optimizer (RPO) to formulate learning path generation as a Markov Decision Process, where a transformer-enhanced Double Deep Q-Network selects optimal concepts while balancing mastery gains and cognitive load. Unlike static systems, our approach replaces conventional assessments with multimodal competency vectors and translates RPO recommendations into personalized learning modules via cross-modal retrieval. The CLKG ensures the system remains current with legal developments, while the RPO tailors pathways to individual gaps, creating a closed-loop adaptive learning environment. Experiments with synthetic and real-world legal education datasets demonstrate that ALL outperforms fixed-path competency models in both knowledge retention and adaptability to legal updates. This work bridges the gap between personalized education and dynamic legal landscapes, offering a scalable solution for lifelong learning in law.

title: SudoPHASE: A Multithreaded Hybrid ACO-SA Sudoku Solver with Ring and Random Communication Topologies
abstract: Sudoku solving is a combinatorial constraint satisfaction problem that becomes increasingly difficult for large grids and low-clue puzzles. In this paper, SudoPHASE is introduced as a parallel hybrid Sudoku solver that combines constraint propagation, the Ant Colony System (ACS), and Simulated Annealing (SA) within a multithreaded architecture. This work integrates multithreaded hybrid ACO–SA with ring-based and randomized communication topologies for coordinated parallel search. Each thread executes an independent solver and communicates through ring-based exchanges of iteration-best solutions and randomized exchanges of best-so-far solutions. We propose a three-source pheromone update mechanism that integrates local and shared information while preserving search diversity. Experimental results on 9×9, 16×16, and 25×25 Sudoku instances demonstrate that the proposed approach improves robustness, convergence speed, and scalability compared to non-hybrid and non-parallel baselines, particularly for large, low-clue puzzles.

title: A Score-Based Framework for AI Text Detection with Adaptive Thresholding
abstract: Currently, many zero-sample AI text detection methods mainly rely on probabilistic scoring mechanisms. However, whether these methods remain reliable when dealing with texts of different language distributions still lacks sufficient research. For instance, the writing of non-native speakers (Non-Native Speakers, NNS) may form language patterns different from those in the training data. This study proposes a scoring-based Adaptive Thresholding Framework to evaluate the performance of the Binoculars detection algorithm under different language distributions. The experimental data includes 180 academic texts, consisting of 60 texts written by native speakers, 60 texts written by non-native speakers, and 60 texts generated by AI. To fairly compare different text types, we choose to dynamically adjust the detection threshold based on the target misclassification rate. Specifically, when setting the misclassification rate of the target language texts to α, we calculate the corresponding adaptive threshold and measure the deviation of the algorithm by comparing the misclassification rates of non-target language texts and target language texts. The experimental results show that the sensitivity of the detection algorithm to language distribution changes is closely related to its underlying dual large language model structure. When using Qwen2.5 as the Performer–Observer combination and setting α = 0.05, the misclassification rate of non-native language texts is significantly higher than that of the target language texts (difference of 0.233), indicating that this model is more likely to misclassify non-native writing as AI-generated texts. Conversely, when using Falcon-7B combination, the difference between the two is significantly reduced, and the statistical results are even close to zero. Additionally, we also tested the fixed threshold (0.901) proposed in the original study. In our experimental process, this threshold cannot correctly identify any AI texts, indicating that the fixed threshold is unstable in different text environments and is difficult to directly transfer for use. The stability of the AI text detection system largely depends on the model architecture. This study demonstrates that dynamic threshold calibration is necessary for improving the effectiveness of NLP detection systems in practical applications.

title: AI-Enabled Voice Replication for Scalable and Personalized Education
abstract: The rapid growth of digital learning environments has increased the need for accessible, personalized, and inclusive educational solutions that cater to learners across diverse linguistic and geographical contexts. Conventional educational content delivery relies largely on manual voice recordings and text-centric materials, which limit scalability, reduce learner engagement, and pose significant challenges for visually impaired students and multilingual classrooms. This paper introduces EduClone, an AI-powered voice intelligence platform that integrates Text-to-Speech (TTS), Speech-to-Text (STT), real-time translation, voice cloning, and voice isolation within a unified architecture tailored for educational applications. The proposed system employs transformer-based speech encoders, multilingual translation models, and deep neural speech synthesis techniques to automatically generate high-quality voice content in 11 Indian languages and over 50 additional global languages, while supporting low-latency streaming.Experimental evaluations demonstrate that EduClone achieves a 32% reduction in content creation time, a 28% improvement in comprehension levels among multilingual learners, and a 40% decrease in operational production costs compared to traditional recording-based workflows. The system’s scalability, robustness, and real-time performance were validated through user evaluation studies and classroom-level deployments. Overall, the findings provide empirical evidence that multimodal speech technologies significantly enhance accessibility, learner engagement, and academic outcomes in modern educational settings, while positioning EduClone as a practical and scalable framework for AI-driven voice-based learning.

title: SHAPE: Unifying Safety, Helpfulness and Pedagogy for Educational LLMs
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely explored in educational scenarios. We identify a critical vulnerability in current educational LLMs, pedagogical jailbreaks, where students use answer-inducing prompts to elicit solutions rather than scaffolded instructions. To enable systematic study, we unify and formalize safe, helpful, and pedagogical behaviors with a knowledge-mastery graph and introduce SHAPE, a benchmark of 9,087 student-question pairs for evaluating tutoring behavior under adversarial pressure. We propose a graph-augmented tutoring pipeline that infers prerequisite concepts from queries, identifies mastery gaps, and routes generation between instructing and problem-solving via explicit gating. Experiments across multiple LLMs show that our method yields significantly improved safety under two pedagogical jailbreak settings, while maintaining near-ceiling helpfulness under the same evaluation protocol. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/MAPS-research/SHaPE

title: Multimodal prediction of visual improvement in diabetic macular edema using real-world electronic health records and optical coherence tomography images
abstract: Multimodal learning has the potential to improve clinical prediction by integrating complementary data sources, but the incremental value of imaging beyond structured electronic health record (EHR) data remains unclear in real-world settings. We developed a multimodal survival modeling framework integrating optical coherence tomography (OCT) and EHR data to predict time to visual improvement in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME), and evaluated how different ophthalmic foundation model representations contribute to prognostic performance. In a retrospective cohort of 973 patients (1,450 eyes) receiving anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy, we compared multimodal models combining 22,227 EHR variables with 196,402 OCT images, with OCT embeddings derived from three ophthalmic foundation models (RETFound, EyeCLIP, and VisionFM). The EHR-only model showed minimal prognostic discrimination (C-index 0.50 [95% CI, 0.45-0.55]). Incorporating OCT improved performance, with the magnitude of improvement depending on the representation. EHR+RETFound achieved the strongest performance (C-index 0.59 [0.54-0.65]), followed by EHR+EyeCLIP (0.57 [0.52-0.62]) and EHR+VisionFM (0.56 [0.51-0.61]). Multimodal models, particularly EHR+RETFound, demonstrated improved risk stratification with clearer separation of Kaplan-Meier curves. Partial information decomposition revealed that prognostic information was dominated by modality-specific contributions, with OCT and EHR providing largely distinct signals and minimal shared information. The magnitude of OCT-specific contribution varied across foundation models and aligned with observed performance differences. These findings indicate that OCT provides complementary prognostic value beyond structured clinical data, but gains are modest and depend strongly on representation choice. Our results highlight both the promise of multimodal modeling for personalized prognosis and the need for rigorous, context-specific evaluation of foundation models in real-world clinical settings.

title: A Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Multi-Agent Framework for Personalized Path Planning in AI Talent Development
abstract: Personalized learning has long been a central goal in educational technology, yet most existing approaches focus on short-horizon adaptation such as next-item recommendation or concept-level mastery estimation. AI talent cultivation poses a broader problem: personalized planning must jointly consider curriculum constraints, prerequisite structure, competency gaps, practical projects, and target job requirements. To address this problem, this paper presents a knowledge graph-enhanced multi-agent framework for personalized path planning in AI talent development. The framework constructs a heterogeneous graph spanning courses, knowledge points, competencies, projects, and job roles, and couples it with four coordinated agents for student profiling, capability diagnosis, path planning, and feedback updating. On this basis, path generation is formulated as a graph-constrained dynamic optimization problem that balances job fit, capability-gap reduction, learning efficiency, and planning cost while supporting replanning when learner state or target role changes. Experiments and case analyses based on program training plans, course syllabi, and AI recruitment requirements show that the framework can generate feasible and job-aligned cultivation paths, respond coherently to dynamic updates, and provide inspectable explanations through graph traces. The study offers an explainable and practically grounded technical route for differentiated AI talent cultivation.

title: Perception and Analysis of Classroom Interaction in Chinese Language and Literature via a Multimodal Generative Alignment Model
abstract: Classroom interaction plays a critical role in the effectiveness of Chinese language and literature education; however, accurately perceiving and analyzing interaction behaviors remains challenging due to the heterogeneity and complexity of multimodal classroom data. To address this issue, this paper proposes a classroom interaction perception and analysis method based on a multimodal generative alignment model. The proposed framework jointly models textual, acoustic, and visual modalities collected from real classroom scenarios, and employs a generative alignment mechanism to learn cross-modal semantic consistency and interaction dynamics. By integrating multimodal feature encoding with generative representation alignment, the model effectively captures both explicit interaction patterns and implicit pedagogical cues in teacher–student and student–student communications. Experimental results on a multimodal Chinese language and literature classroom dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms several baseline approaches in terms of interaction perception accuracy and semantic consistency across modalities. The results indicate that the proposed approach provides a reliable and scalable solution for intelligent classroom analysis and offers practical support for data-driven teaching evaluation and instructional improvement.

title: A Novel Approach to Part-of-Speech Tagging for Kannada Proverbs by using an Optimized Multi-Layer Perceptron
abstract: Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging is a foundational task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), supporting higher-level applications such as Named Entity Recognition (NER), Machine Translation (MT) and Information Retrieval (IR) etc. Kannada proverbs are traditional sayings that convey cultural wisdom and moral lessons. Tagging these kind of words are highly challenging as they are idiomatic, figurative and carry richest collections of linguistic traits. For a language like Kannada, which is basically low resourced and agglutinative in nature, the traditional approaches such as rule-based models and statistical systems have limited ability in capturing contextual meaning and fail in noisy or morphologically rich language settings. Although deep learning architectures Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (BiLSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), transformers achieve state-of-the-art performance, they demand heavy computation and memory, which restricts their use in low-resource environments. This paper proposes an optimized Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) based PoS tagging framework for Kannada proverbs, which is lightweight, faster, and efficient while maintaining competitive accuracy and it is the first attempt in Kannada language history to try out PoS tagging for Kannada proverbs. The proposed model is empirically tested with manually attributed proverb datasets and able to achieve an accuracy of 98%.

abstract: Operating system specialization is a well-known approach to optimize a specific application's performance, memory usage, security, or other important metrics. Specializing an OS for an application is typically a manual process that requires great expertise. Specialization through configuration lends itself well to automation; however, it is challenging due to the sheer size of the configuration space of modern OSes, the difficulty to quantify that space, the long time it takes to evaluate a configuration, and the large number of invalid configurations. Hence, existing attempts at specializing OSes automatically are limited to switching features on and off to minimize memory consumption or attack surface, and cannot target metrics such as performance.

title: Shadow-Q: A Polymorphic, Chaos-Driven Lattice Framework for Unconditional Post-Quantum Cryptographic Secrecy
abstract: Shadow-Q is a new post-quantum cryptographic algorithm that introduces “Polymorphic Hybrid Cryptography,” combining a 7-dimensional hyper-chaotic non-linear system with Ephemeral Entangled Lattice Matrices (E2LM). Unlike static lattice-based NIST PQC standards (e.g., Kyber, Dilithium), Shadow-Q creates algebraic structures that mutate at the microsecond level. Simulated tests against classical and quantum attacks claim unconditional mathematical security, with a 74% reduction in key-storage requirements and a 22% boost in throughput in high-entropy environments.

title: Assignment-Driven Reasoning Optimization: A Dynamic Optimal Assignment Paradigm for Large Reasoning Model Training and Inference
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) typically rely on long-chain reasoning processes to improve performance in complex tasks, but this process is often accompanied by significant redundant computations and structural inefficiencies. Existing methods mainly optimize from the perspectives of pruning, length penalties, or external control, lacking fundamental modeling of the "reasoning structure generation mechanism." This paper proposes a novel training and tuning paradigm: Assignment-Driven Reasoning Optimization (ADRO). This method, for the first time, systematically introduces classical assignment problem theory into reasoning trajectory modeling, reformulating the reasoning process as a dynamic bilateral optimal matching problem: the optimal assignment between the "set of reasoning steps" and the "set of semantic functions/reasoning roles." In this framework, the model no longer directly generates linear thought chains, but instead learns to construct an optimizable assignment matrix, constraining each reasoning step to be the optimal bearer of a certain "functional role," thus naturally suppressing redundant reasoning paths. We further propose a differentiable relaxed assignment mechanism coupled with inference budget Lagrangian optimization, enabling end-to-end training of this framework. This paradigm explains and solves the "overthinking" problem from a structural perspective, essentially transforming the generation problem of LRM into a structural optimal matching problem rather than a sequence generation problem.

title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework Using Random Forest for Predicting Cultural Acceptance of AIGC-Based Yao Ethnic Costume Design
abstract: Yao ethnic costumes are an embodiment of historical memory, belief systems, and survival wisdom, possessing both physical and spiritual attributes. Their rich humanistic aesthetic connotations such as sublimity, natural beauty, and integrated beauty provide important cultural resources for digital regenerative design. Conventional costume culture is entering an intelligent regeneration stage due to the development of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC). It requires the need for data-driven evaluation of public cultural acceptance and inheritance willingness. This paper proposed an explainable machine learning framework to predict public willingness to receive and use Yao ethnic costumes under AIGC regenerative design. This work uses questionnaire data that includes demographic information, cultural identity, aesthetic perception, technology acceptance, and willingness to pass on tradition. Several machine learning (ML) algorithms were implemented for the predicting whether a respondent will show willingness to inherit and use Yao ethnic costumes through AIGC. To improve interpretability, this work uses the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method to analyse feature contributions and explain the internal decision mechanisms of the optimal model. Experimental results show that Random Forest algorithm outperforms well among all algorithms. The research outcomes provide guidance for protecting digital heritage, intelligent costume design, and cultural dissemination strategies.

title: Embedding Information Security in GenAI-Supported Intelligent Robot Teaching: Evidence from a Vocational Course Reform
abstract: This study reports a course reform for an Intelligent Robot System course in higher vocational education that combines generative AI support with explicit information-security training. Implemented with NAO and Pepper platforms, the reform organized learning around three pairings: online theory with offline practice, conventional robot programming with AI-assisted coding, and foundational exercises with project-based innovation. A 16-week single-group pretest-posttest study involving 24 sophomore students examined changes in robot-development performance, programming-task efficiency, and security awareness. After the intervention, robot-development scores increased from 56.2 to 78.5 (t(23)=7.23, p<0.001), average task-completion time decreased from 120 to 72 minutes, and security-awareness scores increased from 2.8 to 4.2 on a 5-point scale (t(23)=8.12, p<0.001). Student feedback indicated that AI support reduced the difficulty of moving from graphical programming to Python-based robot development, but also confirmed the need for teacher guidance, code verification, and secure-use routines. The findings suggest that vocational robot teaching benefits most from structured AI integration that is pedagogically scaffolded and security-aware.

title: Research on the Application of Multimodal Large Language Models in Grammar Correction in English Teaching Scenarios
abstract: To address the issues of insufficient accuracy in grammar correction and the limited feedback methods in English teaching, this study introduces a multimodal large language model into the English teaching scenario, exploring its application value in intelligent grammar correction and teaching assistance. With the Transformer as the core architecture, combined with pre-trained language models and the multi-modal information fusion mechanism, through encoding, multi-feature fusion and decoding processes, a grammar correction model suitable for the English teaching environment is constructed. This research not only enhanced the accuracy and adaptability of the error correction system, but also provided a feasible path for personalized grammar teaching, immediate feedback, and learning process support. It has practical significance for promoting the development of intelligent English teaching. The experimental results show that when using the method proposed in this paper to identify 500 English expressions, the number of correct identifications is 483, which is much higher than that of the other three methods. When dealing with frequent and common errors, the coverage of the research method is better. The coverage of subject-verb agreement errors reaches 98.2%, significantly higher than the comparison methods. When dealing with low-frequency and complex errors, the research method has prominent advantages. The coverage of complex clause structure errors is 94.7%, and the coverage of incorrect use of subjunctive mood errors is 93.2%.

title: Intelligent Laptop Assistance Chatbot using Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: The growth of e-commerce has led to an increasing demand for smart and scalable customer support systems. Traditional chatbots remain less effective since they are more prone to giving incorrect responses due to poor contextual understanding and brittle rule-based reasoning. This paper proposes the use of a Retrieval-Augmented-Generation based laptop assistance chatbot that effectively combines semantic search with large language models powers to provide smart, context-sensitive responses to troubleshoot laptops of top few brands . Product guides and support documents are chunked, processed, and stored in a vector database to enable real-time retrieval. Given a customer's query, the chatbot retrieves the most relevant chunks of documents and leverages a large language model to generate human-like answers. Moreover, the system supports smart recommendations of YouTube videos relevant to the user's question, which enhances guidance over troubleshooting and product usage. The proposed model was evaluated with the RAGAS metric, achieving a faithfulness of 0.81, answer relevance of 0.76, and context precision and recall of 0.74, to show strong factual grounding and contextual reliability. Overall, the system greatly improves response accuracy, reduces human-agent load, and enhances customer experience in resolving laptop related issues.

title: Comparison of the accuracy of selected sentiment analysis tools with psychologists’ evaluations
abstract: This article focuses on a comprehensive evaluation of three available tools—online services (ChatGPT, Google Cloud NLP, and NLP Cloud)—for determining sentiment from text. Currently, there is a strong emphasis on understanding not only the content of the text but also the manner (style and method) in which it is written, especially in interpersonal communication. We input 20 texts with varying sentiment tones into these services using an interface. Additionally, ten psychologists examined the texts to clearly determine, from a professional and human perspective, the feeling each text evokes in a reader. From the results, we observe insignificant differences in the scores among the tools investigated. The highest score was achieved by the Google Cloud tool (0.14), while the lowest scores were achieved by the NLP Cloud (0.10) and ChatGPT (0.09) tools. The highest score of variability was identified for NLP Cloud (0.97). Statistical results simultaneously imply that there is no statistically significant difference in the sentiment scores among individual psychologists for the positive sentiment level, according to Google Cloud results. The evaluations of individual psychologists collectively form one homogeneous group in terms of the sentiment score for the positive level, according to Google Cloud results. While repeated-measures tests were non-significant and confidence intervals overlapped across tools in our corpus, these findings indicate within-sample similarity rather than general interchangeability. We therefore refrain from interchangeability claims and interpret the results as no detected differences in this dataset, conditional on the texts, domains, and scoring scale used.

title: Segmentation-guided knowledge distillation framework for interpretable breast cancer classification
abstract: Abstract Despite the great advances in the clinical diagnosing system, breast cancer is still the most common and fatal disease to woman all over the world, which indicates that there is still a urgent demand of precise and explainable diagnosis system. In this work, we propose a segmentation-guided knowledge distillation framework, which combines the high accuracy of deep learning and clinical explanation ability for breast cancer detection on ultrasound images. The proposed method utilizes a teacher–student framework, and the ResNet-50 teacher is capable of transferring high-level diagnostic representations to the MobileNetV2 student model. Segmentation masks are used as an auxiliary input to guide the student to attend to the tumor areas during training and to improve the relevance of features. This combination provides a good balance for knowledge transfer with low computational complexity. Tested on the BUSI ultrasound dataset, the model outperformed traditional CNN and transfer learning baseline with an overall accuracy and F1-score of 94%. Furthermore, scalability studies demonstrated robust results for reduced fractions of the dataset with real-time inference at more than 200 FPS. The results suggest that distillation of segmentation to the classification task, in the proposed framework improves diagnostic ability and enhances the model explainability, hence it leads to robust and trustworthy AI solutions for breast cancer screening.

title: Improving Infinitely Deep Bayesian Neural Networks with Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Method
abstract: As a representative continuous-depth neural network approach, stochastic differential equation (SDE)-based Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) have attracted considerable attention due to their solid theoretical foundations and strong potential for real-world applications. However, their reliance on numerical SDE solvers inevitably incurs a large number of function evaluations (NFEs), resulting in high computational cost and occasional convergence instability. To address these challenges, we propose a Nesterov-accelerated gradient (NAG) enhanced SDE-BNN model. By integrating NAG into the SDE-BNN framework along with an NFE-dependent residual skip connection, our method accelerates convergence and substantially reduces NFEs during both training and testing. Extensive empirical results show that our model consistently outperforms conventional SDE-BNNs across various tasks, including image classification and sequence modeling, achieving lower NFEs and improved predictive accuracy.

title: Noise-Free Quantum Compilation: Structured Output Distributions on NISQ Hardware Without Mitigation
abstract: Author's note — September 2026: I put this paper up during a period when I was overzealous — I'm disabled and I use AI due to my disability, and I was too trusting of a hallucinating model while I was still trying to figure things out. I've learned a great deal since (I'm building my own models now), and I've come back to restrict what doesn't hold up scientifically, leaving up only what's tangible. I apologize for what shouldn't have gone up in the first place. — Richard Vigslist. Experimental results from the NuviraQ quantum circuit compiler demonstrating that structured, repeatable probability distributions can be produced on IBM NISQ hardware without noise mitigation, error correction, post-selection, or variational feedback. Results span 19 tests and 100+ circuit executions across three IBM QPU backends (Fez, Torino, Marrakesh), including multi-peak distributions in 4-qubit harmonic detection and 90% two-state concentration in 8-qubit entangling chains. Cross-backend variance held below 1.1% with 96-hour temporal stability across four IBM calibration cycles. Challenges the prevailing assumption that runtime mitigation is a prerequisite for structured output on current quantum hardware.

title: Automated Quantum Error Correction Code Selection via Noise Profile Analysis: Bias Detection, Correlation Awareness, and Resource-Optimal Recommendation
abstract: Selecting the optimal QEC code requires expertise in both hardware noise and multiple code families. We present an automated engine that takes raw error rates, classifies noise, detects bias (Z/X asymmetry ratio) and correlated burst errors, and recommends the optimal code with minimum distance and resource estimate. The decision tree maps Z-biased noise to repetition codes, correlated burst noise to color codes, very low rates to Steane codes, and general noise to surface codes. Integration with FTQC resource estimation provides total physical overhead. We demonstrate up to 52.5x reduction in physical qubit count compared to default surface code selection when noise exhibits strong bias.

title: Data Large Model Analysis Framework Driven by Causal Modeling and Experimental Validation
abstract: To address the problems of low analytical efficiency, insufficiently intuitive reasoning logic, and low credibility of analytical results in traditional data analysis methods when handling cross-domain and multi-source heterogeneous data, this paper proposes a large-model analysis framework constrained by structural causal graphs. The framework deeply integrates domain causal rules into the model reasoning process, thereby achieving positive guidance and effective control over the direction of reasoning. A comparative experiment is conducted using a simulated unmanned aerial vehicle reconnaissance effectiveness attribution analysis scenario. The experimental results verify that the proposed framework can effectively reduce the uncertainty of large models in complex causal reasoning tasks and significantly improve the reliability and interpretability of analytical results. The proposed method provides an interpretable intelligent enhancement technical pathway for the automated analysis of cross-domain and multi-source heterogeneous data.

A comparative experiment is conducted using a simulated unmanned aerial vehicle reconnaissance effectiveness attribution analysis scenario. The experimental results verify that the proposed framework can effectively reduce the uncertainty of large models in complex causal reasoning tasks and significantly improve the reliability and interpretability of analytical results. The proposed method provides an interpretable intelligent enhancement technical pathway for the automated analysis of cross-domain and multi-source heterogeneous data.

title: Design of an Adaptive Knowledge Structure Constructing Method for Advanced Mathematics Based on Generative Intelligence
abstract: Fixed representations of sophisticated mathematics knowledge cannot fully capture the hierarchical relationships, pre-requisite relationships and individual differences related to cognition of learners. In order to solvei this problem, this study proposes an adaptive construction method of knowledge structure based on generative intelligence. The proposed method combines ontology-based knowledge encoding, symbolic expression representation, graph dynamic updating and multi-source learning behavior analysis. Simultaneous modeling of concept relations and learner mastery states using a structural space that contains math concepts, formulas, answers to exercises, learning trajectories, dwell time and error patterns. Based on this, the node association, edge weight, weak knowledge connection and personalized learning path are dynamically reconstructed. The experimental results reveal that the proposed method can obtain 90.8% accuracy, 3.2% higher than GKT and 12.3% higher than BKT method. The improvement of learning is 18.1%, the completion time and cognitive load are reduced, compared to conventional learning paths. The results show that the method promotes the adaptability of the structure, weak nodes identification, and can effectively support the intelligent instructional intervention of complex mathematical knowledge system and personalized advanced learning.

title: Image Sentiment Analysis Algorithms and Public Opinion Guidance in Visual Communication
abstract: Addressing the challenges of quantifying image affective information and the lag in public opinion guidance within visual communication, this study constructs a multi-level affective analysis algorithm integrating ResNet and Transformer. The approach incorporates hierarchical feature extraction, including low-level visual encoding, mid-level semantic parsing, and high-level sentiment embedding, allowing more explicit modeling of emotional cues embedded in visual content. Furthermore, a dynamic regression mechanism is employed to capture the temporal coupling between sentiment fluctuations and public opinion intensity, while a risk threshold–based regulation model enables adaptive intervention strategies under rapidly evolving opinion dynamics. Experiments conducted on AffectNet and T4SA datasets (62,400 total samples) demonstrate 92.4% recognition accuracy and an F1 score of 91.3%, representing a 6.6% improvement over traditional architectures. Testing within real-world public opinion scenarios further confirms the model's capability to suppress negative sentiment propagation through iterative adjustment of dissemination rhythm and semantic restructuring. Negative sentiment diffusion rates decreased by 22%, and fluctuations in opinion intensity reduced by 19%. Overall, the integration of sentiment recognition, temporal prediction, and risk-driven regulation forms a closed-loop framework that enhances the stability, interpretability, and responsiveness of sentiment management in visual communication environments.

title: GR: a fixed-frequency time series data timestamp compression algorithm based on RLE
abstract: The existing time-series data compression algorithms do not fully consider the specific case of time-series data with fixed frequency. When the time-series data is compressed, the general compression algorithms are still used, resulting in a certain degree of information redundancy. Based on this, a GR (Gorilla_RLE) timestamp compression algorithm for fixed frequency sequential data is proposed based on Gorilla compression algorithm. First, obtain the first order differential value of the timestamp of each data point; Then, obtain the second order differential value of the timestamp, and adopt a corresponding compression strategy based on the data distribution of the second order differential value; Finally, RLE encoding is performed on consecutive and identical second-order difference values. Experiments on publicly available datasets show that the proposed method can compress the timestamp of fixed frequency sequential data more effectively than Gorilla and other compression algorithms, and the larger the fixed frequency sequential dataset, the higher the compression rate.

title: Emotion Detection from Text Using TF-IDF and Logistic Regression: A Hybrid NLP Framework with Real-Time Deployment
abstract: Sentiment analysis is critical to text mining due to rapid text data growth. Sentiment analysis is utilized to track social media, rate customer opinions, diagnose mental diseases, and understand how humans talk to computers. Most emotion-detecting methods today center around non-text inputs, but come on, much of what we learn about humans online is text-based. Therefore, the goal of this project is to develop a system with AI that detects emotions from text. The proposed system uses natural language processing (NLP) techniques and machine learning models to classify emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, fear, and surprise, among others, from textual input.. It incorporates rule-based methods, sentiment, and context-sensitive tools aiding emotion detection. It employs some incredible advanced natural language processing technology such as sentence transformers, and BERT-like models to accurately pin down neutral sentiments Evaluation metrics, including accuracy, F1 score, and recall, demonstrate the effectiveness of the model, highlighting its potential for real-world deployment. The findings suggest that AI-based emotion analysis from text holds promise for improving human-computer interaction and enabling more emotionally responsive applications They test it on public sentiment analysis corpora, and the experiments prove that our model is better than current approaches in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall. This just shows how great AI-based emotion analysis is inimproving the way we communicate with computers and creating apps that can understand emotions.

title: Seeing the Whole Elephant: A Benchmark for Failure Attribution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Failure attribution, i.e., identifying the responsible agent and decisive step of a failure, is particularly challenging in LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) due to their natural-language reasoning, nondeterministic outputs, and intricate interaction dynamics. A reliable benchmark is therefore essential to guide and evaluate attribution techniques. Yet existing benchmarks rely on partially observable traces that capture only agent outputs, omitting the inputs and context that developers actually use when debugging. We argue that failure attribution should be studied under full execution observability, aligning with real-world developer-facing scenarios where complete traces, rather than only outputs, are accessible for diagnosis. To this end, we introduce TraceElephant, a benchmark designed for failure attribution with full execution traces and reproducible environments. We then systematically evaluate failure attribution techniques across various configurations. Specifically, full traces improve attribution accuracy by up to 76\% over a partial-observation counterpart, confirming that missing inputs obscure many failure causes. TraceElephant provides a foundation for follow-up failure attribution research, promoting evaluation practices that reflect real-world debugging and supporting the development of more transparent MASs.

title: Data-Free Contribution Estimation in Federated Learning using Gradient von Neumann Entropy
abstract: Client contribution estimation in Federated Learning is necessary for identifying clients' importance and for providing fair rewards. Current methods often rely on server-side validation data or self-reported client information, which can compromise privacy or be susceptible to manipulation. We introduce a data-free signal based on the matrix von Neumann (spectral) entropy of the final-layer updates, which measures the diversity of the information contributed. We instantiate two practical schemes: (i) SpectralFed, which uses normalized entropy as aggregation weights, and (ii) SpectralFuse, which fuses entropy with class-specific alignment via a rank-adaptive Kalman filter for per-round stability. Across CIFAR-10/100 and the naturally partitioned FEMNIST and FedISIC benchmarks, entropy-derived scores show a consistently high correlation with standalone client accuracy under diverse non-IID regimes - without validation data or client metadata. We compare our results with data-free contribution estimation baselines and show that spectral entropy serves as a useful indicator of client contribution.

title: Neuro-Edu: A Cognitive Science-Driven Framework for Large Language Model Alignment in Educational Sandbox Simulation
abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in educational contexts demands a fundamental reconceptualization of alignment methodologies, moving beyond generic helpfulness optimization toward pedagogically-grounded cognitive alignment. This technical whitepaper presents Neuro-Edu, a comprehensive framework that synthesizes principles from cognitive science—specifically cognitive load theory, dual-process reasoning models, self-regulated learning theory, and schema theory—with state-of-the-art LLM alignment techniques to create adaptive educational sandbox simulations. Unlike prior approaches that treat alignment as an orthogonal concern to educational effectiveness, Neuro-Edu operationalizes cognitive science principles as explicit alignment objectives, enabling LLMs to dynamically calibrate explanation complexity based on real-time cognitive load estimation, promote both intuitive and analytical reasoning through systematic scaffolding strategies, and support progressive transfer of regulatory control from system to learner. Extensive experiments across mathematical reasoning, scientific explanation, and programming education domains demonstrate that Neuro-Edu achieves statistically significant improvements over baseline alignment approaches, with a 47.3% increase in knowledge retention rates, 69.2% improvement in transfer learning outcomes, and 55.1% enhancement in metacognitive engagement scores. title: Cultural Anchor Loss and Related Failure Patterns in Large Language Models: Evidence from Spanish Popular Culture
abstract: This paper introduces Cultural Anchor Loss (CAL) as a distinct failure mode in large language models, separate from factual hallucination. CAL occurs when a model fails to detect that a given expression either lacks a single unambiguous referent or requires specific cultural anchoring beyond statistical association. Instead of suspending judgment and requesting clarification, the model produces a confident, plausible, but incorrect response. We present empirical evidence from a structured evaluation of 12 cases drawn from Spanish popular culture (music lyrics, advertising slogans, television catchphrases, and real broadcast events), tested against GPT-4.5 and GPT-5. We also describe a taxonomy of ten related phenomena observed during the evaluation, of which Cultural Anchor Loss is proposed as the primary failure mode from which several others derive.Este artículo introduce la Pérdida de Anclaje Cultural (Cultural Anchor Loss, CAL) como un modo de fallo específico en los modelos de lenguaje de gran escala, distinto de la alucinación factual. El CAL se produce cuando un modelo no detecta que una expresión dada carece de un referente unívoco o requiere un anclaje cultural específico más allá de la asociación estadística. En lugar de suspender el juicio y solicitar aclaración, el modelo produce una respuesta segura, plausible pero incorrecta. Se presenta evidencia empírica a partir de una evaluación estructurada de 12 casos extraídos de la cultura popular española, probados con GPT-4.5 y GPT-5, junto con una taxonomía de diez fenómenos relacionados.

title: Audio Processing Techniques for Voice Cloning and Information Extraction from Audio Files
abstract: Voice cloning has become a rapidly evolving field in artificial intelligence and speech processing. Recent advances in deep learning have made it possible to replicate human voices with remarkable accuracy using relatively small datasets. At the core of this technology lies the ability to analyze and interpret audio signals in order to capture the unique characteristics of a speaker’s voice. Audio files contain a wide range of information including speech content, speaker identity, emotional state, pronunciation patterns, and environmental context. Extracting and modeling this information is essential for developing effective voice cloning systems. Modern voice synthesis frameworks rely on several stages of audio signal processing including signal acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction, representation learning, and neural speech generation. This paper presents a comprehensive study of how audio signals are processed in voice cloning systems and explores the various types of information that can be extracted from audio recordings. The research examines the structure of digital audio signals, the methods used to convert sound waves into machine-readable data, and the feature extraction techniques that capture acoustic properties of speech. In addition, the paper investigates modern neural architectures used for voice cloning such as spectrogram-based models, neural vocoders, and speaker embedding networks. The study also highlights several practical applications of voice cloning technologies including digital assistants, personalized speech synthesis, accessibility tools, and entertainment systems. Furthermore, the research discusses ethical considerations and potential risks associated with voice cloning technologies, emphasizing the need for responsible development and robust detection mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that audio signals contain rich multi-layered information that can be effectively utilized to develop advanced speech synthesis and analysis systems

title: A Multi-Layer Security Defense Framework for Industrial Intelligence
abstract: The rapid evolution of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is reshaping industrial cybersecurity. While generative artificial intelligence enables defense capabilities such as threat detection, vulnerability mining, and security operations, it also introduces new risks through malicious uses like automated attacks and deepfakes. Existing studies often focus on a single dimension, lacking systematic analysis of full-lifecycle risks and holistic defense strategies for industrial scenarios. This paper proposes a five-dimensional risk framework covering computing power, data, model, application, and compliance governance, along with a matching three-layer collaborative defense system of technology, management, and governance, offering theoretical and practical guidance for industrial risk prevention in the GAI era.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Affect Aware Content Adaptation in Intelligent Tutoring Systems
abstract: Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) have advanced in personalized learning, but their ability to adapt to learners' emotional states is limited. This paper proposes an emotion-aware content adaptation framework using Reinforcement Learning (RL). A lightweight CNN extracts facial expressions and emotional features from video streams, which are then integrated with cognitive data. A Deep Q-Network (DQN) dynamically adjusts content difficulty, presentation, and pacing to enhance long-term learning outcomes. This approach enables personalized learning experiences based on students' emotional states (such as frustration or boredom), making intelligent tutoring systems more interactive and adaptive, thereby enhancing students' emotional satisfaction and long-term learning outcomes. This framework offers a novel solution for emotion-driven adaptive teaching in intelligent tutoring systems.

title: A Review of Large Language Models for Cybersecurity Defense: Core Capabilities, Application Practices, and Challenges
abstract: The rapid evolution of cyber threats — characterized by advanced persistent threats (APTs), software supply chain attacks, and AI-driven adversarial payloads — has exposed fundamental limitations in traditional rule-based and signature-based defense mechanisms. Large Language Models (LLMs), with core capabilities spanning natural language understanding, code engineering, logical reasoning, and autonomous decision-making, offer a transformative paradigm for cybersecurity defense. This paper presents a systematic review of LLM applications across the entire cybersecurity defense lifecycle. The review begins with an analysis of the core capabilities and key enabling technologies of LLMs — including prompt engineering, domain fine-tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and agent frameworks — that underpin their adaptation to security tasks. Application practices are then examined across four critical stages: pre-attack prevention and secure development (covering vulnerability detection, secure code generation, supply chain security, and malware/phishing detection), during-attack detection and threat awareness (including network intrusion detection, log analysis, and threat intelligence automation), post-attack response and disposition (encompassing digital forensics and automated incident response),. The paper further dissects the security risks inherent to LLMs themselves — such as prompt injection, jailbreaking, data poisoning, and model stealing attacks — along with corresponding defense technologies. Finally, key challenges are identified, including hallucination, real-time performance bottlenecks, domain knowledge scarcity, data silos, interpretability deficits, and compliance risks, with future research directions proposed toward building more robust, trustworthy, and human-centered intelligent defense systems.

title: Prompt-Based Emotion Detection and Story Generation
abstract: Emotion recognition from text and story generation with aligned emotions are still difficult tasks in natural language processing because of the imbalance problem, the overlap of emotions, and the open-ended nature of creative text generation. This paper proposes a hierarchical emotion-aware framework that combines super-sentiment classification, fine-grained emotion recognition, data augmentation, and story generation based on prompts in a single pipeline. The proposed system involves three-class super-sentiment classification and fine-grained emotion recognition using RoBERTa-based transformer models trained on the EmpatheticDialogues dataset. To handle the imbalance problem, a controlled data augmentation approach that leverages paraphrasing, back translation, and semantic filtering is used. Experimental results show that the proposed super-sentiment classifier has an accuracy of 71.86%, and the ablation study validates the effectiveness of the hierarchical labeling approach and controlled data augmentation. The predicted emotional states are then used with a GPT-2 language model using structured prompt conditioning for story generation with aligned emotions without any additional fine-tuning. A discussion on computational complexity and generative evaluation underscores the feasibility and limitations of the proposed framework. The proposed architecture effectively integrates emotion understanding and creative text generation for emotion-aware NLP applications.

title: Artificial intelligence enhances cancer cell selection for HER2 gene amplification assessment in breast carcinoma
abstract: The evaluation of HER2 gene amplification is a time-consuming process that requires quantifying a large number of signals in cancer cells to ensure reproducible results, a task that can be assisted by image analysis (IA) tools. This study aimed to develop and validate an artificial intelligence-based cancer cell detection model for detecting breast carcinoma in bright-field in situ hybridization (ISH) whole-slide images, with the goal of improving cancer cell selection prior to the quantification of HER2 and CEP17 gene copies. The difference in IA performance was not statistically significant compared to visual assessment in quantifying the HER2/CEP17 ratio and average HER2 copy numbers per cell. However, IA with the Cancer Cell Detection Module (IA 2.0) quantified consistently higher values than IA without (IA 1.0). Cancer cell detection in IA 1.0 showed 64% sensitivity, 83% specificity, and a positive predictive value (PPV) above 95% for samples with at least 84% cancer cellularity. IA 2.0 improved cancer cell detection sensitivity to 69% and specificity to 93%, achieving a PPV above 95% for samples with at least 66% cancer cellularity. IA 2.0 showed 95% concordance with visual scoring (k = 0.90), with 90% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Discordant cases required the selection of a second cancer cell-enriched region of interest, shifting classification from HER2-negative to HER2-positive. After correction, IA 2.0 achieved full agreement with visual classification (100%, k = 1.000), underscoring the critical role of the pathologist supervision in this assay.

title: Fast Neural-Network Approximation of Active Target Search Under Uncertainty
abstract: We address the problem of searching for an unknown number of stationary targets at unknown positions with a mobile agent. A probability hypothesis density filter is used to estimate the expected number of targets under measurement uncertainty. Existing planners, such as Active Search (AS) and its Intermittent variant (ASI), achieve accurate detection but require costly online optimization. To reduce online computation, we propose to use a convolutional neural network to approximate AS or ASI decisions through direct inference. The network is trained on AS/ASI data using a multi-channel grid that encodes target beliefs, the agent position, visitation history, and boundary information. Simulations with uniform and clustered target distributions show that the network achieves detection rates comparable to AS or ASI while reducing computation by orders of magnitude.

title: Deep Neural Network-guided PSO for Tracking a Global Optimal Position in Complex Dynamic Environment
abstract: We propose novel particle swarm optimization (PSO) variants incorporated with deep neural networks (DNNs) for particles to pursue globally optimal positions in dynamic environments. PSO is a heuristic approach for solving complex optimization problems. However, canonical PSO and its variants struggle to adapt efficiently to dynamic environments, in which the global optimum moves over time, and to track them accurately. Many PSO algorithms improve convergence by increasing the swarm size beyond potential optima, which are global/local optima but are not identified until they are discovered. Additionally, in dynamic environments, several methods use multiple sub-population and re-diversification mechanisms to address outdated memory and local optima entrapment. To track the global optimum in dynamic environments with smaller swarm sizes, the DNNs in our methods determine particle movement by learning environmental characteristics and adapting dynamics to pursue moving optimal positions. This enables particles to adapt to environmental changes and predict the moving optima. We propose two variants: a swarm with a centralized network and distributed networks for all particles. Our experimental results show that both variants can track moving potential optima with lower cumulative tracking error than those of several recent PSO-based algorithms, with fewer particles than potential optima.

title: Desenvolvimento de Confiança e Perseverança em Robótica Educacional com Aprendizagem Baseada em Projetos
abstract: Este artigo apresenta os resultados de um programa de robótica educacional voltado a estudantes do ensino fundamental da rede pública, desenvolvido com a metodologia de Aprendizagem Baseada em Projetos (ABP). As oficinas buscaram promover o desenvolvimento de competências em programação, eletrônica e construção de robôs, além de investigar os efeitos sobre a confiança e a perseverança dos participantes. A pesquisa foi conduzida com abordagem mista (qualitativa e quantitativa), por meio de questionários aplicados ao longo das atividades. Os resultados apontaram aumento na autoeficácia dos estudantes em circuitos eletrônicos e programação, e estabilidade na construção de estruturas físicas e mecânicas. O uso de recursos como protocolos, rubricas, mini-lições e webquests contribuiu para o engajamento e para a consolidação do aprendizado. O programa demonstrou potencial para aproximar a educação tecnológica da comunidade escolar e estimular o interesse pela continuidade dos estudos em cursos técnicos integrados.

title: Gauberte Fabricio de Vagad, el antiguo autor de la Celestina.
abstract: Análisis Estilométrico del Manuscrito II-1520: Autoría y Atribución en el Taller de Zaragoza (ca. 1498): Gauberte Fabricio de Vagad Descripción (Abstract) Este repositorio contiene los resultados y la metodología del estudio estilométrico realizado sobre el manuscrito II-1520 de la Biblioteca de Palacio, empleando el software JGAAP (Java Graphical Authorship Attribution Program). La investigación aplica el algoritmo de Burrows Delta sobre n-gramas de caracteres ($n=6$) y un análisis de los 200 eventos más frecuentes para desentrañar la compleja red de autoría oculta tras las atribuciones tradicionales del siglo XV. Los datos obtenidos demuestran una convergencia estadística irrefutable hacia la figura de Gauberte Fabricio de Vagad y el círculo de la Oficina de los Lucena en Zaragoza. Los resultados sitúan a Vagad como el arquitecto sintáctico del texto, escoltado por un joven Fernández de Oviedo, cuyo perfil actúa como alumno aventajado y ejecutor estilístico dentro del taller de Paulo Hurus. El estudio revela una estructura de "escuela de escritura" donde la sofisticación humanista (reflejada en la proximidad con el control de Bembo) desplaza definitivamente la autoría administrativa de Fernando de Rojas, quien aparece en posiciones de marginalidad estadística (puesto 22, $\Delta > 250$). Este hallazgo es fundamental para la historiografía literaria, ya que identifica el manuscrito II-1520 como el eslabón perdido entre la tradición de Juan de Mena y la modernidad renacentista, gestada en los laboratorios de prosa de la Corona de Aragón. Metodología y Herramientas Software: JGAAP (Burrows Delta). Parámetros: N-gramas de 6 caracteres, 200 eventos más comunes, normalización de espacios en blanco y unificación de mayúsculas. Corpus de Referencia: Perfiles maestros de Fernández de Oviedo, Gauberte Fabricio de Vagad, Luis de Lucena, Hernán Núñez el Pinciano y otros autores contemporáneos del periodo 1470-1530. Fuente Primaria: Transcripción paleográfica del Manuscrito II-1520 (Biblioteca de Palacio).

title: Heisenberg Limited Liquid Networks: Solver‑Free Neural Dynamics via Phase‑Space Uncertainty
abstract: We propose Heisenberg-Limited Liquid Networks (HLLN 2.1), a recurrent neural architecture that achieves continuous-time, liquid dynamics without numerical ODE solvers. By grounding state updates in a learnable uncertainty principle, the network modulates its own temporal integration rate in response to input surprise. HLLN 2.1 uses 75–80% fewer parameters than Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) while matching or exceeding performance on chaotic time-series forecasting, regime-shift adaptation, and character-level language modelling. The architecture exposes an interpretable “Metabolic Friction” signal that correlates with environmental instability, providing built-in uncertainty quantification. All code is available at github.com/Kshitiz-Maurya/HLLN2.1.
