title: Construction of an AI-Enabled Evaluation Model for Ideological and Political Course Teaching Effect Based on Machine Learning and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP)
abstract: This paper focuses on the evaluation of teaching effectiveness in ideological and political courses. In response to the limitations of traditional evaluation methods and combined with the application trend of AI technology in the field of education, it constructs an AI-enabled evaluation model for ideological and political course teaching effectiveness based on machine learning and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Firstly, it introduces the basic principles of machine learning, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and its advantages, as well as the relevant theoretical foundations of the teaching effectiveness evaluation system. Secondly, it elaborates on the model design ideas, including the principles and basis for constructing the evaluation index system, the AHP-based weight allocation method, and the process of data collection and preprocessing. Then, by comparing and analyzing different machine learning algorithms, it selects the final algorithm, expounds the parameter tuning strategy, builds the experimental environment, details the experimental procedure, and visualizes and interprets the results. Next, it demonstrates the application of the model in actual teaching scenarios through case analysis, compares teaching effectiveness before and after application, collects and analyzes student feedback, and discusses the challenges encountered in the implementation process and corresponding countermeasures. Finally, it summarizes the research findings, reviews the main conclusions, explains the significance of this study for the reform of ideological and political course teaching, points out the deficiencies of the current model, and proposes future improvement plans and broader application prospects.

title: Intelligent Analysis System of College Students' Behavior Based on Data Mining
abstract: With the continuous construction of the smart campus system, colleges and universities have put forward higher intelligent and personalized requirements for student behavior management and services. However, the current intelligent perception and control technology has significant deficiencies in the continuity of behavior data collection, the accuracy of behavior pattern recognition, the dynamic update capability of individual portraits, and the real-time nature of resource recommendation, making it difficult to meet the diversified development needs of students. To this end, this paper proposes to deeply integrate artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things to build an intelligent analysis system for college student behavior. The system collects multi-dimensional data such as students' card access, library stay time, canteen consumption frequency, dormitory return time, and teaching building entry and exit behavior in real time through Internet of Things devices, and combines K-means clustering, principal component analysis (PCA) and long short-term memory network (LSTM) to model behavioral characteristics and predict trends. Based on the above model results, an adaptive recommendation engine is further designed to accurately push personalized course resources, work and rest improvement suggestions, and campus activity notifications based on students' learning preferences and behavioral habits. Experimental results show that after introducing the AIoT fusion model, the frequency of student library use increases by 28.7% compared with the baseline, the utilization rate of course resources increases by 26.7%, the frequency of late return behavior decreases by 22.4%, and the click-through rate of recommended content reaches 42.3%, achieving high-resolution identification of student behavior and refined improvement of university services.

title: Multilingual Refusal Alignment for Safer Large Language Models
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are deployed globally, ensuring their safety and alignment across multiple languages becomes paramount. However, safety behaviors often vary unpredictably between languages, posing significant challenges for consistent and ethical AI. In this work, we systematically investigate the dynamics of multilingual alignment, exploring whether single-language alignment transfers cross-lingually, how language consistency is preserved during training, and the resulting trade-offs with general knowledge capabilities. We introduce RefusEU, a novel refusal alignment dataset covering 12 European languages, including a dedicated test set for evaluating current state-of-the-art models. Our controlled Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) experiments provide two key insights: aligning models exclusively in English is insufficient to ensure cross-lingual safety, even for the same harm categories, whereas training on multilingual datasets can improve safety without degrading general performance, as measured by the Global MMLU benchmark.

title: Practical Quantum CIM Empowerment via All-Domestic-Core Agentic Large Model
abstract: Quantum computing devices are recognized as powerful tools for solving NP-complete problems. However, the intricacy of their modeling presents notable barriers for non-specialists, while the tedious iteration of constraint weights and modeling methodologies also consumes substantial effort on the part of experts. To address these challenges, this study integrates a femtosecond laser-pumped Coherent Ising Machine (CIM) with an LLM-driven agentic system by leveraging the LangGraph and LangChain frameworks. Comprehensive investigations demonstrate that large language models (LLMs) can effectively perform such tasks in modeling as QUBO/Ising model calibration, constraint weight decision iteration and rapid validation of literature-reported schemes. Notably, all these tasks can be fully implemented based on domestic large models, combined with domestically developed CIM hardware, we truly achieve the practical empowerment of quantum CIM that fully relies on all-domestic agentic large models and hardware. This work successfully realizes robust technological integration, laying a solid foundation for subsequent research. Nevertheless, it also identifies the persisting challenges in the two cutting-edge fields of large models and quantum computing at the current stage. Encouragingly, we unexpectedly discover a promising new paradigm where accumulated knowledge from agent-assisted quantum computing iterations reciprocally enhances the agent's own problem-solving capability, thereby addressing these challenges.

title: Energy-Efficient Federated Learning with Temporal Convolutional Networks for Intrusion Detection
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has significantly increased the attack surface of modern network infrastructures, necessitating intelligent and scalable intrusion detection systems. Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for distributed model training without centralized data sharing; however, challenges such as energy efficiency, data heterogeneity, and privacy preservation remain inadequately addressed. Existing studies often emphasize optimization objectives theoretically without validating them under realistic constraints. This paper proposes an energy-aware federated learning framework integrating Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) for intrusion detection using distributed network traffic data. The framework incorporates differential privacy for secure model updates and a conceptual energy-aware client participation strategy. Experiments are conducted on the UNSW-NB15 dataset under a controlled setting with fixed client participation and communication parameters. title: The underlying logic and innovative development path of artificial intelligence technology
abstract: Since the beginning of the 21st century, artificial intelligence technology has developed at an unprecedented speed, gradually permeating into every aspect of our lives, from voice assistants on smartphones to autonomous vehicles, from medical diagnosis to financial analysis. Artificial intelligence has become an important force driving social progress. Artificial intelligence may seem both familiar and mysterious. We use the conveniences it brings every day, but rarely delve into its underlying logic and innovative development path. In fact, the development of artificial intelligence is not achieved overnight, but is built upon a complex and stable technical system, simultaneously influenced by various factors such as market demand, policy guidance, and ethical constraints. A deep understanding of the underlying logic and development path of artificial intelligence not only helps us better adapt to future society but also stimulates our interest and contemplation in technological innovation. With the continuous evolution of technology, artificial intelligence is no longer just a concept in scientists’ laboratories, but has truly entered thousands of households and become an indispensable part of modern life. It has changed our learning methods, communication modes, and even ways of thinking, and its influence is continuously expanding.

title: Artifact: Tool Paper: AGTix: Concise Definition of Scope Graphs in Reference Attribute Grammars
abstract: This artifact accompanies the tool paper 'AGTix: Concise Definition of Scope Graphs in Reference Attribute Grammars' of Luke Bessant and Eric Van Wyk, submitted to ACM SIGPLAN SLE 2026. Its purpose is to demonstrate the use of AGTix constructs for specifying the construction and interrogation of scope graphs, which are implemented as a language extension to the reference attribute grammar language Silver. AGTix is a fusion of Statix (inspiration for the constructs introduced is primarily inspired by MiniStatix) and reference attribute grammars (Silver specifically), which brings Statix-like constraints for building and querying scope graphs into RAGs as new equation forms, implemented as a language extension to Silver. This allows a much more concise definition of scope graph-based name analysis than is yielded by the full Statix-to-RAGs translation of our previous work. The new AGTix constructs implicitly translate to attribute declarations/definitions and production equations akin to what is presented in that previous work, hiding the details such as how targets of edge assertions are propagated around an AST, which often involve many more equations and definitions than what AGTix specifications yield. It also means that Statix specifications can be more easily translated to RAG specifications, as a consequence of AGTix is that these now have a much closer line-to-line correspondence. The artifact contains a number of example languages with name resolution semantics defined using AGTix, scripts for compiling those languages, and other scripts for executing each with test input programs which compare output against expected results. Packaged with this artifact are the Silver Jarfiles for the latest version of AGTix.

title: Unified Quantum-Safe Security Platform with Noise Reachability Analysis and Enhanced QKD Eavesdrop Detection
abstract: We present QCrypton v4.0, extending the unified quantum-safe security platform with two major capabilities: (1) a Quantum Noise Reachability Engine that classifies noise into 12 sub-types, evaluates against 6 QEC codes (720 evaluations), and recommends optimal correction with 24 compensating controls; and (2) enhanced BB84 eavesdrop detection via statistical noise decomposition, demonstrated catching an eavesdropper at 9.8 sigma when standard BB84 reported "secure." The platform now comprises 12 scanners, post-quantum crypto (FIPS 203/204/205), FTQC cost estimation (28 algorithms), noise reachability, code scanning (6 languages), and automated remediation — all via CLI/SDK/API with zero third-party crypto dependencies.

title: Reward-Guided Dynamic Fusion and Modality Decoupling for Enhanced Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) integrates multiple modalities to better understand human emotions. However, existing methods often neglect heterogeneity among modal features, causing redundancy and inconsistencies. Additionally, the dynamic interplay between modalities is frequently ignored during fusion, limiting performance. To address these issues, we propose Reward-Guided Dynamic Fusion and Modality Decoupling (RDFD). RDFD includes two key components: (1) a feature decoupling module that separates modality-specific and modality-shared features, reducing redundancy and conflicts; (2) a Reward-Guided Dynamic Fusion module that adaptively selects guiding modalities to enhance modality-specific representations and enable flexible fusion. Experiments on the CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI datasets show that RDFD achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in advancing Multimodal Sentiment Analysis.

title: Assessing Machine Translations of Advertising Slogans: A Pilot Study with Human Evaluation and BLEURT Scores
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have made significant advancements in natural language processing tasks, particularly in translations. Existent studies have explored their performance in translation of domains such as idioms, however, there is limited research which focuses on translation of advertising slogans. This pilot study aims to investigate the feasibility of applying DeepSeek-V3.2 in translation of skincare product slogans and evaluate the model performance when it is instructed with four prompt templates. The evaluation is conducted by two practicing translators supplemented by the automatic metric BLEURT. The findings suggest improvement in translation qualities with the prompts as measured by human judgement. Preliminary evidence suggests that translation outputs could be better than others when prompts include consumer information, though the observation remains tentative. However, according to BLEURT scores, the model could perform better than baseline-prompted translations only when instructed with prompts consisting of brand names. Significant divergences in their rankings reflect discrepancies between evaluation criteria of human annotators who prioritize cultural adaptability and linguistic appropriateness, and BLEURT which focuses on semantic similarities and fluency.

title: Design and Application of Intelligent Feedback System for English Writing Based on BERT and Learning Analytics
abstract: Aiming at the problems of heavy manual correction workload, strong subjectivity, and delayed feedback in college English writing teaching under the background of educational digitalization, this paper designs and implements an intelligent writing feedback system based on BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) and learning analytics. The system constructs a rigorous multi-dimensional feature engineering framework, which explicitly extracts and quantifies lexical features (e.g., type-token ratio), syntactic features (e.g., sentence complexity), discourse coherence, and semantic completeness. To ensure methodological rigor, this study conducts three layers of experimental verification: a large-scale model comparison experiment, an ablation study to validate feature design, and a 16-week controlled teaching quasi-experiment with statistical significance tests. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed BERT-based model achieves an accuracy of 92.4%, which is significantly superior to traditional machine learning baselines. In the teaching experiment, the group using the proposed system achieved a 12.5% increase in writing scores and a 53.8% reduction in grammatical errors (p<0.001). The system provides a feasible technical solution for the digital transformation of English writing evaluation.

title: A Computational Approach to Service Quality Mining in Mobile Reading Applications Using LDA Topic Modeling and SnowNLP Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This study presents an integrated computational framework combining Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling and SnowNLP sentiment analysis to systematically mine service quality insights from Chinese user reviews of mobile reading applications. We collected 7,991 reviews from three major platforms operating under different business models (Tomato Novel, QiMao, Qidian) via the Tencent MyApp marketplace and applied systematic text preprocessing including jieba word segmentation, part-of-speech tagging, and stopword removal, yielding 4,741 valid samples (59.3% retention rate). The LDA model with optimized hyperparameters (α=0.1, β=0.01, k=5) achieved excellent coherence (C_v=0.5430), identifying five service dimensions: Payment/Monetization (47.6%), Advertising (21.7%), Content Ecosystem (19.8%), Content Quality (6.1%), and Authors (4.8%). Notably, business model topics dominate user attention (69.3% vs 30.7% content-related), challenging the traditional "content is king" paradigm. Sentiment analysis revealed 60.8% positive reviews (mean=0.6261), with advertising showing surprisingly positive sentiment (0.73, 72.7% positive rate), suggesting user acceptance of ad-supported free models. Cross-platform comparison demonstrates Tomato's ad-supported model (0.7252) significantly outperforms QiMao's hybrid (0.5017) and Qidian's premium subscription (0.4967) approaches. This framework demonstrates unsupervised text mining efficacy for service quality assessment and provides actionable insights including optimal ad frequency (1-2 ads/chapter) and duration (5-15 seconds) thresholds for platform optimization.

title: Soil Data Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Large Language Models
abstract: Abstract This study examines the applicability of large language models for automated data extraction from soil-science research papers, using a corpus of Russian-language articles from the journal Pochvovedenie/Eurasian Soil Science (2019–2020). Extraction quality was evaluated using GPT-4 Turbo’s answers to a set of 58 questions covering characteristics of research objects and conditions, soil types, measurement methods, and measurement results. Automated and expert-based approaches to assessing the correctness of the model’s answers were compared. The aim was to evaluate how well large language models (LLMs) can extract and verify data from scientific articles. The baseline model’s outputs were compared with expert gold-standard annotations, deterministic metrics based on lexical overlap, and the scores of several alternative language models acting as independent “judges.” The integrated F1 score for individual questions was at least 0.73, while the mean values across thematic question groups reached 0.91–0.99. The correlation between the most consistent judge model Gemini 2.5 Flash and expert ratings reached 0.8 and explained about 60% of the variance in expert assessments, whereas classical n-gram metrics were significantly less informative. These results indicate that LLMs are promising as the basis of a scalable pipeline for the automated construction of soil property databases and reducing manual effort in the analysis of scientific texts.

title: Attention-Based Deep Learning for Medical Insurance Cost Prediction: A Comparative Analysis of TabNet and Tabular Transformers
abstract: We need accurate estimates of healthcare insurance costs so that we can set fair prices and use our resources wisely. The lack of use of attention-based methods in the study of healthcare tabular data, even though they have great potential, makes premium valuation models less accurate and harder to understand. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of attention-based models in comparison to conventional baseline models for forecasting medical insurance costs. We used 1338 de-identified health insurance information to test five models: linear regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, as well as TabNet and a Tabular transformer. We used the root mean squared error and the coefficient of determination to see how well it worked. A notable finding from the analysis of the results is that about 60.69 percent of the total significance is due to smoking-related factors. In conclusion, the suggested research utilizing attention-based models offers interpretability advantages that are beneficial in healthcare settings and comparable to strong tree-based standards. The analysis and forecasts that come from this are helpful for making decisions and setting prices in a clear way.

title: An Algorithm for On-Sensor Agnostic Detection of Changes in Human Activity for Ultra-Low-Power Applications
abstract: Wearable devices running Human Activity Recognition(HAR) on Inertial Measurement Units~(IMUs) waste energy by performing continuous classification for each window, even during long periods of unchanged activity. We address this with a lightweight change-detection gate: a non-parametric algorithm based on dynamic template matching that runs continuously at only approximately 16kFLOPs per step, requires no offline training, and does not need prior definition of target activity classes. The gate invokes the full HAR network only when it detects an activity change, reducing the computational load by over 67% in realistic monitoring settings. The algorithm is evaluated on smart glasses, smartwatch, and smartphone data, requiring only a brief device-specific calibration phase. The gate achieves 98% sensitivity on UCA-EHAR, ensuring no genuine activity transition is missed, while 75% specificity keeps unnecessary HAR invocations low. Results on WISDM are 97% sensitivity and 76% specificity, demonstrating robustness and flexibility to various settings.

title: SS-MOM-XAI: A Responsible AI Governance Framework for AI-enabled Service Ecosystem (AISE)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in AISE, extending from user encounters to organisational coordination and institutional oversight. In such layered structures, explanation failures cannot be reduced to algorithmic opacity alone; rather, they often arise from sociotechnical misalignments among AI-mediated decision-making, organisational responsibilities, and accountability structures. To address this gap, this study proposes SS-MOM-XAI as a methodological framework for operational human-centred AI in AISE. The framework reframes explainability from a modular property to distributed AI governance in service. The SS-MOM-XAI comprises five core components: SS architecture, MOM hierarchy, approach taxonomy, analytical framework, and product-service design method. Empirically, the framework is applied to two contrasting ecosystems: the Fresh Flower Retail Delivery Service Ecosystem (FFRDSE) and the Bluetooth Charging Service Ecosystem for New Energy Vehicles (BCSEfNEV). Cross-case findings indicated that governance depth increases with domain risk and that explanation obligations must be distributed across service layers. The study makes the following main contributions: it proposes the SS-MOM-XAI framework for human-centred AI in AISE. It provides systematic guidance for analysing and designing for understandability in real service ecosystems. Furthermore, provides an implementation strategy with actionable recommendations through a three-phase model that spans the design projects.

title: PEDAGOGICAL MODEL FOR MANAGING INDIVIDUAL EDUCATIONAL DIRECTIONS BASED ON INTERACTIVE PEDAGOGICAL SOFTWARE TOOLS
abstract: This article covers the theoretical and practical foundations of managing students' individual educational programs (IEDs) using interactive pedagogical software tools (IPDQ). It is substantiated that the modern educational paradigm requires a personality-oriented approach, which, in turn, leads to the need to adapt the content of education to the needs, abilities, and pace of assimilation of the student. Based on the analysis of the architecture of adaptive learning systems, foreign (RWTHmoodle, FLIC) and national platforms, the article proposes a pedagogical model for designing ITB through IPDQ.

title: MCFS: LLM Reasoning Method Based on Multi-Level Constraints and Multi-Source Fusion Beam Search
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have exhibited strong capabilities in language understanding and generation for open-domain question answering. However, they still suffer from widespread knowledge scarcity and hallucination issues in multi-hop factual reasoning scenarios, which affect the accuracy of reasoning results. The Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG) paradigm can effectively make up for this defect and improve the reliability and interpretability of generated answers. Nevertheless, existing KG-RAG methods have obvious limitations: they either ignore the importance of graph structural information or neglect the relevance between relations and question semantics, ultimately restricting the accuracy of multi-hop reasoning. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces MCFS, an LLM reasoning method that integrates multi-level constraints with multi-source fusion beam search, whose core goal is to achieve effective alignment among question semantics, LLM prior knowledge, and graph structural information. Specifically, first, we innovatively propose to generate multi-level constraints based on LLMs, providing precise guidance by extracting semantic constraints from questions; second, we train a semantically guided edge-level graph neural network (GNN) to model relation relevance; then, we innovatively propose a multi-source fusion beam search strategy to explore reliable reasoning paths; finally, we leverage explicit reasoning paths to guide LLMs in generating interpretable answers. Experimental results on standard knowledge graph question answering benchmarks show that MCFS consistently outperforms strong baselines and delivers the best overall performance.

title: Empathetic Gamified Feedback for English Learners: A Lightweight Reward Calculator with Dynamic Sentiment Adaptation
abstract: This paper propose a novel Reward Calculator system that generates empathetic, gamified feedback for English learners while minimizing data dependency. The system integrates psycholinguistic analysis with lightweight transformer models and reinforcement learning to dynamically adapt feedback based on real-time emotional and linguistic cues. Unlike conventional approaches, our method avoids extensive user profiling by employing a sentiment-aware analyzer to extract emotional valence and linguistic complexity, which then condition a dynamic reward generator to produce human-like responses. Furthermore, the system embeds gamification directly into the reward calculus, enabling seamless progression tracking without auxiliary modules. The proposed architecture combines DistilBERT for efficient sentiment analysis and GPT-2 Small for feedback generation, ensuring scalability and low-latency interaction. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves higher emotional resonance and linguistic accuracy compared to static reward functions. This work bridges the gap between affective computing and language learning, offering a practical solution for real-time conversational practice with minimal data overhead. The approach is particularly significant for applications where user privacy and computational efficiency are critical constraints.

title: Research on Topic Modeling and Evolution Analysis of Sci-tech Literature Based on Multi-data Source Fusion
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has demonstrated strong potential in the fields of text mining and knowledge discovery. The core issues currently faced by the topic modeling and evolution analysis of scientific and technological literature include shallow semantic understanding, difficulty in multi-source fusion, low topic quality, rough evolution analysis, low computational efficiency, and insufficient cross-language support. This study proposes a framework for topic modeling and evolution analysis of scientific and technological literature based on multi-source data fusion. By introducing Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers for Topic Modeling In addition to BERTopic, it combines cross-source mid-term fusion strategies to enhance topic consistency, interpretability, and the accuracy of evolution tracking. The experimental results show that the topic consistency score of the proposed method on the literature dataset in the field of artificial intelligence reaches 0.71, and the topic diversity is 0.89. Compared with the traditional Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model method, it is improved by more than 40%. And after expert verification, it successfully identified emerging frontier topics such as "AI-enabled scientific discovery" and "neuro-symbol fusion". Overall, this framework has achieved effective improvements in the accuracy of topic discovery and the reliability of evolution tracking. It provides an effective intelligent analysis solution for scientific research trend detection and decision support.

title: Cognitive-aware dual-state fusion network for knowledge tracing
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) aims to predict students’ future performance by analyzing their learning records. Although existing deep learning-based KT models have achieved notable progress in inferring students’ knowledge states and forecasting upcoming performance, it remains challenging to model learners’ behaviors and cognitive processes with sufficient granularity. This paper proposes CaDSKT (Cognitive-aware dual-state fusion network for knowledge tracing), leveraging deep learning techniques to achieve more comprehensive and accurate estimation of learners’ cognitive states. Specifically, the authors design a dedicated deep representation module for problem-solving states and introduce a hybrid attention mechanism (parallel–fusion) to effectively capture complex cognitive dynamics throughout the learning process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model substantially outperforms existing approaches in prediction accuracy and knowledge-state modeling capability. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness and synergy of the individual components.

title: A Multimodal Deep Learning Approach for Emotion-Aware Speech Recognition
abstract: The following research proposes an integrated Deep Learning pipeline that unifies speech recognition, natural language understanding, and emotion-aware analysis to achieve human-like comprehension of spoken interactions. The system initiates with the fine-tuning of OpenAI's Whisper model by LoRA-based parameter-efficient training on the LibriSpeech ASR dataset for high-quality, lightweight speech-to-text transcription. The model performance was evaluated against metrics such as WER, CER, and BLEU score for linguistic fidelity. Subsequently, the resultant text is subjected to several steps involved in a multi-stage Natural Language Processing framework about Glove embedding, an Autoencoder, and then a Bidirectional GRU-based RNN for extractive summarisations, while a Keyword CNN highlights semantically important terms. The most relevant sentences, identified by the RNN, are passed to advanced transformer models such as Google Gemini and T5 for abstractive summarization, yielding coherent, context-rich summaries of conversations. In parallel, the system includes an emotion recognition module trained on the RAVDESS dataset using MFCC features extracted with torch audio and modelled through both MLP and GRU architectures. By analyzing pitch variation and RMS energy, the system maps detected emotions into expressive "vibe" categories such as enthusiastic, frustrated, hesitant, or calm, providing an additional emotional layer to dialogue understanding. Together, these components create a comprehensive AI framework capable of transcribing speech, understanding its semantic essence, summarizing key information, and interpreting emotional tone, forming a foundation for the next generation of emotionally intelligent and context-aware conversational systems.

title: Quantum interference of distinguishable photons based on spatially resolved measurements
abstract: We present experimental results demonstrating the quantum interference of two photons distinguishable in their transverse momenta, each entering the input ports of a balanced beam splitter. This counterintuitive interference effect is made possible through spatially resolved measurements in the near field, i.e., by resolving the conjugate variable in which the photons are distinguishable. Our experimental findings agree with theoretical predictions. We contrast our results with a non-spatially resolved measurement where averaging over the photons' positions washes out the quantum interference observed in spatially resolved measurements.

title: Spiritual-Emotion Guided Fine-Tuning of Mistral-7B for Mental Health Conversational Systems using Bhagavad Gita Knowledge
abstract: Abstract—Artificial intelligence–based conversational agents have recently gained attention as scalable solutions for mental health assistance. Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate strong language understanding and generation capabilities; how- ever, their responses in counseling contexts often lack emotional grounding, empathy, and philosophical reasoning required for sensitive mental health interactions. This research proposes a Spiritual-Emotion Guided Mental Health Dialogue System developed using parameter-efficient fine- tuning of the Mistral-7B-Instruct large language model. The proposed system integrates philosophical teachings from the Bhagavad Gita to improve emotional stability, reflective reasoning, and empathetic response generation in mental health conversations. Bhagavad Gita scriptures are extracted from PDF sources using the PDFPlumber framework and converted into structured question–answer instruction pairs for supervised fine-tuning. The base model is adapted using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), enabling efficient domain-specific learning while preserving the general capabilities of the pretrained model. The proposed system is evaluated using a mental health counseling dialogue dataset to assess its effectiveness in generating supportive and contextually meaningful responses. The expected outcomes indicate improved emotional coherence, contextual understanding, and response quality compared to the baseline language model. The findings aim to demonstrate that integrating philosophical knowledge with modern language models can enhance the effectiveness and empathy of AI-driven mental health dialogue systems. Index Terms—Mental Health AI, Mistral-7B, LoRA, Bhagavad Gita, Psych8K, Emotional Intelligence, Parameter Efficient Fine- Tuning

title: Digital pathology and artificial intelligence in breast and gynecologic oncology: from molecular prediction to multimodal integration
abstract: Breast and gynecologic cancers consist of two groups of complex solid tumors, each with unique genomic features, immune microenvironments, and treatment responses. Recent advances in next-generation sequencing, spatial profiling, and digital pathology have transformed diagnostic methods, enabling seamless integration of morphological and molecular data. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are now essential tools for linking histomorphology, immunophenotype, and molecular alterations in ways that were previously unachievable. This review discusses recent progress in integrating digital and molecular pathology for these cancers, with an emphasis on practical clinical applications. We highlight emerging research in breast, endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancers, where combined image-based and molecular approaches can predict treatment response and survival. Additionally, spatial transcriptomics and proteomics are deepening our understanding of tumor heterogeneity and the interactions between tumor cells, stroma, and immune cells that drive disease progression. We also address current challenges, such as standardization, reproducibility, regulation, and workflow integration, and propose priorities to facilitate the clinical adoption of multimodal data.

title: Cross-domain Expression Recognition Based on Feature Alignment and Pseudo-labeling Methods
abstract: Unsupervised domain adaptation, which aims to enhance the performance of models on unlabeled target domains by leveraging labeled source domain knowledge, is a research hotspot in the field of transfer learning. To address the issue of decreased model generalization due to domain shifts in cross-domain emotion recognition, we systematically explore two adversarial domain adaptation methods and three pseudo-label screening strategies to improve the recognition accuracy of the model on the target domain. For feature alignment, the two effective methods are Domain-Adversarial Neural Network (DANN) and Maximum Classifier Discrepancy (MCD). For self-training, we specifically consider three pseudo-label selection strategies: adjusting the confidence threshold, global ranking by confidence, and ranking within each category. The experimental results show that the MCD method achieved a better feature alignment effect; while in the pseudo-label method, the strategy based on the internal ranking of categories performed the best, increasing the accuracy of the ResNet50 model on the target domain from 64.73% to 77.29%, effectively alleviating the class imbalance problem and improving the recall rate for difficult-to-identify categories.

title: Design of an English Teaching Resource Mining System Based on Cloud Computing
abstract: The fragmentation of English teaching resources and their low utilization efficiency have become key factors restricting the digital development of English teaching. The distributed storage and intelligent computing capabilities of cloud computing technology provide technical support for solving this problem. This paper designs an English teaching resource mining system based on cloud computing, which adopts a cloud-management-terminal three-tier architecture to achieve technical separation between data collection and intelligent mining. The cloud-side foundation is built based on the Hadoop/Spark distributed cluster, and the system development is completed with a variety of development tools. A heterogeneous database storage mode is designed to adapt to different types of teaching resources, and multi-source data collection interfaces are developed to realize the comprehensive access of resources. The system achieves four core functions: multi-modal resource parsing, implicit knowledge point mining, dynamic tag clustering and personalized resource recommendation. The performance of the system in terms of resource mining efficiency, accuracy and recommendation matching degree is verified through targeted tests. This system can realize the intelligent mining and efficient utilization of English teaching resources, provide a technical solution for the digital integration and personalized supply of English teaching resources, and adapt to the diversified needs of modern English teaching.

title: Effects of Prompt Formats on Model Thinking: The Impact of CoT Language Complexity on Multi-hop Reasoning
abstract: The pre-trained large-scale language model still faces major challenges in context multi hop reasoning. The design of the prompt format in prompt engineering has emerged as an effective approach to address this issue. This study uses the DeepSeek-R1-8B model and HotPotQA data set as the prototype of prompt words, and tests three prompt formats (plain text, JSON, markdown) under guided and non-guided conditions. The key innovation is to use SpaCy to conduct linguistic analysis on the thinking chain of the model, and quantify the characteristics of cognitive complexity with a suite of multi-dimensional indicators. The results show a clear "mediating effect" path. The guided markdown format can trigger the most hierarchical syntactic structure and has the highest accuracy. Plain text without guidance produces the most focused reasoning, making it effective for comparison tasks. The syntactic tree depth exhibits a significantly positive predictive relationship with accuracy, while the lexical entropy has a significantly negative prediction accuracy. The analysis of this paper can provide a cognitive framework for the design of prompt format for complex reasoning tasks.

title: Multi-baseline interferometric angular estimation under baseline imperfections
abstract: Abstract Precise angular estimation of remote targets is a fundamental task in optical interferometry, particularly in the weak-light regime where photon resources are limited. Interferometric schemes employing multiple telescopes can overcome the diffraction limit of a single aperture but are often highly sensitive to experimental imperfections. In this work, we study a piecemeal interferometric approach that jointly exploits measurement data from multiple baselines for angular estimation, and we relax the constraints on baseline configurations. The proposed scheme remains effective even with a reduced number of baselines, highlighting its practical applicability. Focusing on realistic experimental conditions, we analyze the impact of baseline length and orientation errors on the estimation performance. We show that both the original and generalized piecemeal protocols exhibit strong robustness against these imperfections and achieve higher angular estimation precision than existing single-baseline weak-light interferometric schemes under identical practical conditions.

title: Incomplete multi–view partial multi–label learning network with structure–aware consistent fusion
abstract: In recent years, incomplete multi-view partial multi-label classification has attracted growing attention due to its practical relevance. However, many existing methods rely on equal-weight (average) fusion and thus overlook sample-wise reliability differences across views, making the fused representations vulnerable to noise and missing views. To address this issue, we propose the Structure-Aware Consistency Fusion Network (SACF-Net) for incomplete multi-view partial multi-label classification. SACF-Net assigns instance-level view weights based on structural consistency, following the principle that larger structural deviation implies lower view reliability, which enables fine-grained fusion and improves the structural stability of the fused embeddings. Moreover, we convert the prior graph structure into a prior neighborhood distribution and introduce a graph-guided distribution consistency objective to align the neighborhood distribution induced by the fused representation with the prior one, while encouraging agreement among view-specific neighborhood distributions. This design strengthens multi-view consistency at the neighborhood-distribution level and alleviates missingness-induced distribution shifts. Experiments on five public benchmark datasets demonstrate that SACF-Net consistently outperforms competitive methods on multiple evaluation metrics.

title: Transferable Physical-World Adversarial Patches Against Pedestrian Detection Models
abstract: Physical adversarial patch attacks critically threaten pedestrian detection, causing surveillance and autonomous driving systems to miss pedestrians and creating severe safety risks. Despite their effectiveness in controlled settings, existing physical attacks face two major limitations in practice: they lack systematic disruption of the multi-stage decision pipeline, enabling residual modules to offset perturbations, and they fail to model complex physical variations, leading to poor robustness. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel pedestrian adversarial patch generation method that combines multi-stage collaborative attacks with robustness enhancement under physical diversity, called TriPatch. Specifically, we design a triplet loss consisting of detection confidence suppression, bounding-box offset amplification, and non-maximum suppression (NMS) disruption, which jointly act across different stages of the detection pipeline. In addition, we introduce an appearance consistency loss to constrain the color distribution of the patch, thereby improving its adaptability under diverse imaging conditions, and incorporate data augmentation to further enhance robustness against complex physical perturbations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TriPatch achieves a higher attack success rate across multiple detector models compared to existing approaches.

Specifically, we design a triplet loss consisting of detection confidence suppression, bounding-box offset amplification, and non-maximum suppression (NMS) disruption, which jointly act across different stages of the detection pipeline. In addition, we introduce an appearance consistency loss to constrain the color distribution of the patch, thereby improving its adaptability under diverse imaging conditions, and incorporate data augmentation to further enhance robustness against complex physical perturbations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TriPatch achieves a higher attack success rate across multiple detector models compared to existing approaches.

title: Applications of Machine Learning: Feature Extraction and 3D Anomaly Detection
abstract: This thesis studies the anomaly detection topic in modern manufacturing, primarily focusing on 3D data and novel artificial intelligence techniques. Firstly, this study goes through the literature review of the manufacturing context, 3D datasets of manufacturing processes, and the techniques used in anomaly detection. In the next stage of our research, this study describes the research models with multi-settings and introduces the modification of the DeepMS-based dataset for anomaly detection. Finally, the experimental results prove the potential improvement of quality control systems based on the combination of data generation and anomaly detection.

title: Designing and Governing Trustworthy AI Marketing Systems in Educational Technology: A Managerial and Implementation Framework
abstract: This study proposes a dual-dimensional framework to design such technologies in the EdTech industry using the conceptual framework methodology, which is based on thematic content analysis and theory-driven and evidence-based validation using scholarly literature, industry reports, and policies from the top EdTech organizations worldwide. The framework identifies trustworthiness as the key construct that integrates two interrelated dimensions. The governing dimension is operational at the managerial level and includes governance principles based on an extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) framework and personalization governance principles based on three dimensions, such as intensity, tempo, and boundaries. The designing dimension is operational at the implementation level and identifies the technical requirements related to virtual sales personnel systems and AI promotion systems. The results of the validation process against known platform practices demonstrate a mixed pattern of alignment, with stronger support in regulatory-related areas and weaker support in governance-intensive domains where the framework extends current industry practice. The extension of the UTAUT model from personal acceptance to organizational governance represents a theoretical contribution with a link to existing research in personal acceptance and its expanded applicability. The three-dimensional personalization governance model has more detailed mechanisms than the current one-dimensional approaches. For educational technology organizations, the framework offers systematic guidance in the development of AI-based marketing systems that are trustworthy to users while being effective for organizational goals. Validation results indicate tempo governance and recommendation explainability as areas that need development in the industry for effective engagement with users in a sustainable manner.

title: Design and Implementation of Advanced Deep Q - Network for Robot Motion Control
abstract: The mobile robots are increasing day by day because of their numerous applications. The motion control of these robots is very important to finish a task perfectly. The motion control of robots is to identify a time series of control inputs that will result in the required output or motion. Controlling inputs are typically motor currents, although they can be converted into torque or velocity for control design. A required trajectory, which consists of x and y coordinates, often describes the desired motion. In this research, for robot motion control, the advanced Deep Q-Network (DQN) controller is designed. The performance of the DQN controller in robot motion control is evaluated with the conventional controllers of Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) and Neuro-Fuzzy Controller (NFC). The performance of the controllers is compared using error metrics like Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE), Integral Squared Error (ISE), and Integral Absolute Error (IAE). The two-wheeled mobile robot is used to implement the controller designs. The experimental outcome of the motion control of the two-wheeled mobile robot shows the excellence of the DQN controller with an IAE error of 8.45 in x-coordinate tracking and 5.33 in y-coordinate tracking.

title: Thinking Fast and Slow in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis: A Case Study of Qwen2.5-Omni
abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) aims to predict human emotions by integrating diverse signals such as text, audio, and visual cues. While Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) like Qwen2.5-Omni have demonstrated remarkable end-to-end capabilities in processing heterogeneous data, it remains unclear whether these models process all modalities with equal cognitive efficiency. Drawing inspiration from human cognitive psychology, we investigate the application of System 1 (fast, direct) and System 2 (slow, reasoning-based) thinking strategies in LMMs for MSA. Through extensive evaluations on standard datasets, we discover a stark modality-cognitive gap: highly semantic text modalities excel under System 1 direct inference, whereas noisy, low-level non-verbal modalities (audio and visual) often benefit from the multi-step reasoning of System 2 to prevent catastrophic alignment failures. Furthermore, we observe that forcing System 2 reasoning on simple text inputs leads to an "over-thinking" degradation. Based on these findings, we advocate for an Adaptive Inference approach in LMMs, where cognitive effort is dynamically allocated based on modality complexity.

title: Construction of a Community Resident Consumption Behavior Prediction Model Based on GNN
abstract: Rapid advancements in intelligent algorithms have enabled new approaches for modeling consumer behavior. To overcome the limitations of traditional methods in capturing multi-layered relationships and group interactions, this study proposes a Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based consumption behavior prediction model. Residents, merchants, and consumption categories are represented as heterogeneous nodes, with multidimensional relationships fused through a weighted adjacency matrix. The model integrates traditional Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) structures with attention mechanisms to dynamically weight information propagation and enhance the representation of complex consumption patterns. Using real data from an integrated community service platform in East China, including approximately 12,000 residents and 7.9×10⁶ valid transaction samples, the proposed model achieved 93.1% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.917, outperforming the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Random Forest models by about 5.2% and 7.9%, respectively. For regression tasks, the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) decreased to 17.8 and the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) to 24.6, representing roughly an 8% improvement over traditional GCNs. These results confirm the model's effectiveness in capturing complex consumption dependencies and enhancing predictive performance.

title: Entanglement Enhanced Sensing with Qubits affected by non-Markovian Dephasing
abstract: Entanglement has been proposed as a means to improve the sensitivity of sensing weak signals. While the degree of this quantum advantage is well understood in noiseless settings, the situation is more complex under realistic conditions, where the system is subject to decoherence. In this case, the enhancement depends on the specific noise characteristics. Previous treatments of colored noise typically assume that the noise is uncorrelated between successive experiments. Here, we consider the scenario in which the noise exhibits correlations across multiple shots. We derive a simple fundamental limit to the sensitivity based on the fact that the sensitivity cannot be better than the signal-to-noise ratio seen by the probe. Focusing on Ramsey spectroscopy with probes affected by pure classical dephasing, we show that, for suitable spatial and temporal noise correlations, entangled probes achieve a better scaling of the sensitivity with the number of probes than separable states. This demonstrates that entanglement can provide a substantial improvement for Ramsey spectroscopy subject to correlated noise.

title: The Grover Adaptive Search Algorithm as a Solver: High-Order Unconstrained Binary Optimization Problems
abstract: High-order binary optimization (HUBO) formulation can represent many real world problems. This mathematical approach is particularly relevant within the quantum computation domain because quantum hardware allows to directly map and solve these problems. The thesis explores the implementation of Grover Adaptive Search (GAS) by varying the different free parameters to evaluate the quality of the solution and the success rate of the algorithm, along with a possible optimization procedure. In particular, GAS is an algorithm that is compliant with HUBO and theoretically offer a quadratic speed up over classical computation. This thesis implements a quantum circuit for GAS algorithm to solve a 4-city traveling salesman problem along with two strategies to reduce the gate counts. The results include the output quality of the value of the objective function and the success rate of reaching the true minimum of 7, where the optimal configuration achieves an average value of 9.4 and a success rate of 36%. This configuration also maintains a 7% lower average value and a 10% higher success rate compared to randomly generated parameters.

title: Yksityisyyttä suojaavat menetelmät yhdistetyssä oppimisessa
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an ML scheme where multiple parties collaborate on a task in order to build either a global model or a local model informed by other similar datasets as the local one. One of the main benefits brought by FL is being able to benefit from others’ data without accessing it. Fl may provide solutions to many issues conventional ML faces regarding data privacy, sharing and usage. However there are still unsolved issues and weaknesses FL needs to be provenly resilient against before widespread adoption in critical fields. The purpose of this literature review is to examine the ways an attacker might be able to attack a FL system and what methods can be used to defend against these attacks. Additionally this review discusses FL’s relation to legislation and approaches to explainable FL. The different architectures a FL system can use are also charted and categorized.

title: Behavioral Stability of Quantized Large Language Models Under Prompt Drift: The Resilio Evaluation Framework
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are actively deployed in resource-constrained environments using quantization like 8-bit and 4-bit precision, which reduces memory usage and inference costs. While these models perform well on clean benchmarks, real-world deployment frequently encounters ''Prompt Drift''-typographical errors, informal phrasing, and structural degradation. This paper brings Resilio, a systematic evaluation framework which investigates the interaction of model quantization and five progressive levels of prompt quality degradation. We have evaluated Llama 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B, and Phi-3 Mini using our two novel metrics: the Task Performance Score (TPS) and the Behavioral Stability Score (BSS). These findings challenge assumptions about quantized model frailty and suggest that, for most real world applications, deployment decisions should prioritize model architecture choice and input quality control over quantization level selection.

title: Regional Short-Term PV Power Forecasting Based on Graph Convolution and Transformer Networks
abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for power system scheduling and market operations. Existing studies have shown the value of numerical weather prediction (NWP), graph-based spatial modeling, and temporal sequence learning, but the boundary of their contributions remains fragmented across many practical forecasting frameworks. In particular, adjacent multi-point NWP information is often not explicitly organized according to its spatial relationships, while historical similar-day power is rarely integrated with graph-structured meteorological features in a unified model. To address this gap, this study develops a short-term PV power forecasting framework that combines multi-point NWP graph construction with similar-day-guided Transformer fusion. First, predicted irradiance from the target site and neighboring NWP points is organized as a graph, and a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) is used to extract local spatial meteorological features. Second, similar days are identified through a two-stage selection strategy based on Euclidean distance and Pearson correlation, and the corresponding historical power sequences are aggregated as temporal guidance. Finally, the graph-extracted NWP features, similar-day power, and predicted humidity are fused by a Transformer-based temporal modeling module to generate day-ahead PV power forecasts. Experimental results show that the proposed framework outperforms TCN-Transformer, Transformer, GCN, LSTM, and BP on the studied dataset, and maintains favorable performance on additional PV stations. These results indicate that the joint integration of graph-structured multi-point NWP information and historical similar-day power is effective for short-term PV power forecasting.

title: Exam Samachar: An AI-Driven Decision Support System
abstract: The Exam Samachar — Smart News Analyzer is an innovative AI-driven application designed to automatically interpret, summarize, and evaluate news content from uploaded newspapers, images, or PDF documents. Leveraging Visionbased Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically LLaMA 3.2 Vision via the Ollama framework, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipelines, the system extracts headlines, identifies publication dates, generates structured summaries, and provides contextual insights into political, social, and regional news stories. A built-in sentiment analysis module categorizes each article as positive, negative, or neutral with polarity confidence scores. The system is deployed on a Streamlit-based interactive interface supporting multi-page PDF uploads, page-wise analysis, and multilingual summary generation. Evaluation on 50 newspaper editions demonstrated headline extraction accuracy of 91.4%, sentiment classification F1-score of 0.87, and an average API response time of 5.3 seconds per page. title: A Method for Formulating Fire Accident Emergency Plans Based on Case-Based Reasoning
abstract: In the event of a sudden fire, firefighters need quickly bring the situation under control and minimize casualties and property damage by implementing appropriate and effective emergency response plans. Since the circumstances of each fire incident vary, it is necessary to rapidly develop rescue and response plans tailored to specific fire scenarios. This paper proposes a method for generating initial emergency response plans based on Case-Based Reasoning and Naive Bayes classification. Based on existing emergency response plan data resources, this method employs a Naive Bayes classification algorithm to identify the emergency plan that best matches the specific fire incident scenario, thereby rapidly generating an initial emergency response plan. This paper demonstrates the feasibility of this method through a specific fire case study. This method can enhance the effectiveness of emergency response and the accuracy of rescue operations following a fire incident, providing an effective approach for decision-making in emergency response to sudden fire incidents.

title: Metric Inversion in Generative AI Translation: Divergence Between Automated Evaluation Metrics and Human Expert Judgement in the LRM Era
abstract: The paradigm of computer-assisted translation (CAT) is currently navigating a period of profound structural disruption fueled by Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI). The transition from deterministic Neural Machine Translation (NMT) to reasoning-driven Large Reasoning Models (LRMs), such as DeepSeek R1, has introduced complex chain-of-thought (CoT) capabilities. However, this advancement has precipitated a “Metric Inversion” crisis. Traditional automated evaluation metrics, specifically BLEU and chrF, rely on surface-level n-gram overlap against a static human reference. As AI capability shifts from literal sequence mapping to creative semantic restructuring, these legacy benchmarks systemically penalize the exact linguistic and idiomatic qualities that human experts value most. Through a randomized double-blind study (N = 111), we contrast the performance of an LRM, a general LLM, and a standard NMT system. Results demonstrate that while human experts strongly favor LRM outputs for their superior fluency (Mean=8.81) and idiomaticity (Mean=8.61), automated metrics exhibit a significant and misleading bias toward traditional NMT (BLEU=0.258). Correlation analysis reveals a profound negative relationship (ρ = −0.401, p <.001) between BLEU scores and expert fluency ratings. This research highlights the urgent need for a paradigm shift from reference-dependent overlap matching to semantic-aware evaluation frameworks to preserve the structural integrity of AI-assisted education.

title: A Methodology for Constructing an Intelligent Risk Control System for Financial Shared Service Centers Based on Knowledge Graphs
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, graph computing, and data-driven modeling techniques, financial shared service centers have become large-scale information systems featuring high concurrency, complex process dependencies, and heterogeneous data interactions. Conventional rule-based risk control and single statistical models exhibit limited capability in capturing implicit risk correlations and supporting dynamic decision-making. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a computer-oriented intelligent risk control framework based on knowledge graph modeling. Multi-source financial data are processed through automated entity recognition, relation extraction, and semantic fusion to construct a domain-specific risk knowledge graph. On this foundation, graph-based risk factor identification, structural risk assessment, and hybrid algorithm-driven early warning mechanisms are developed to enable relational reasoning and risk propagation analysis. A prototype system is implemented for experimental validation. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves higher risk recognition accuracy and improved computational efficiency compared with traditional methods, providing an effective and scalable technical solution for intelligent financial risk governance.

title: Pyramid: A Secure, Resource-Efficient, and Pluggable Kubernetes for Multi-Tenancy
abstract: This work aims to achieve the best of both worlds with two prominent techniques adopted in cloud computing systems: hardware trusted execution environments (TEEs) for data processing security, and Kubernetes (k8s) for efficient container orchestration and resource management for multi-tenancy. A secure, resource-efficient, and pluggable container orchestration system, called Pyramid, is proposed, which incurs minimal intrusive modifications to the commercial k8s. Pyramid puts a separate trusted k8s on top of the original k8s cluster and carefully cooperates between the two layers. The workflow within each layer is maximally preserved without significant changes. The untrusted layer manages resource scheduling across different tenants to improve utilization and passes the resource information to the trusted layer to launch actual computations secured by TEEs, with the help of carefully designed interface and protection mechanisms. Evaluation results show that Pyramid achieves 1.4X higher throughput on the data plane, with comparable control-plane performance to previous work.

title: C-MORAL: Controllable Multi-Objective Molecular Optimization with Reinforcement Alignment for LLMs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show promise for molecular optimization, but aligning them with selective and competing drug-design constraints remains challenging. We propose C-Moral, a reinforcement learning post-training framework for controllable multi-objective molecular optimization. C-Moral combines group-based relative optimization, property score alignment for heterogeneous objectives, and continuous non-linear reward aggregation to improve stability across competing properties. Experiments on the C-MuMOInstruct benchmark show that C-Moral consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models across both in-domain and out-of-domain settings, achieving the best Success Optimized Rate (SOR) of 48.9% on IND tasks and 39.5% on OOD tasks, while largely preserving scaffold similarity. These results suggest that RL post-training is an effective way to align molecular language models with continuous molecular design objectives. Our code and models are publicly available at https://github.com/Rwigie/C-MORAL.

title: Heralded Entanglement Transfer from Entangled Atomic Pair to Free Electrons
abstract: We propose a protocol that transfers entanglement from an entangled atomic two-level-system (TLS) resource to a pair of free electrons in an energy-sideband ladder via local electron-TLS interactions. In a controlled rotating-wave regime, closed-form reduced states are derived. TLS heralding then prepares a maximally entangled electron state in a two-dimensional single-excitation manifold, with a simple dependence on the initial TLS resource entanglement. Numerical integration of the full bilinear Hamiltonian quantifies the impacts of detuning and pulse shaping and identifies the leading beyond-rotating-wave corrections. The results establish a heralded route to entangled free electrons and will facilitate further advances in quantum electron optics.

title: It's Time to Standardize RDF Messages
abstract: RDF-based systems increasingly operate in event-driven and streaming settings, where producers and consumers exchange data as discrete units of communication rather than as freely mergeable RDF statements. As existing RDF semantics and tooling do not provide an interoperable notion of what statements belong together as one message, developers often rely on out-of-standard techniques, transport-level assumptions, or heuristics, leading to interoperability problems and inefficiencies. We propose the concept of an RDF Message as an RDF Dataset intended to be interpreted atomically as a single communicative act, laying the foundation for defining RDF Message Streams and RDF Message Logs. The proposal makes message boundaries explicit across serializations, transport, and storage systems, which in turn enables incremental consumption and reproducible replay in use cases such as IoT observations, archived RDF streams, nanopublications, or processing SPARQL CONSTRUCT results. Building on this, RDF Message Profiles, such as Linked Data Event Streams or ActivityStreams, then provide the terms for describing pagination, message structure, ordering, or retention policies. As part of the W3C Community Group on RDF Stream Processing, we are now seeking broader support and comments on the proposal from the Semantic Web community.

title: Toffoli-porttien toteutuskustannuksien alentaminen approksimaatioilla
abstract: The Toffoli gate (controlled-controlled-NOT) and its multi-controlled generalizations are fundamental logical building blocks of quantum algorithms and utilized extensively in pivotal algorithms such as Grover’s algorithm and Shor’s algorithm. Despite being a fundamental logical primitive of quantum algorithms, Toffoli gates must be decomposed to primitive single-qubit and two-qubit gates which are available in physical quantum hardware. These decompositions incur significant implementation costs in circuit depth and gate count, costs that propagate directly to the entire circuit. Consequently, reducing the implementation cots of Toffoli gates provides a direct method of reducing the implementation costs of many quantum algorithms. This thesis evaluates state-of-the-art methods for reducing the implementation costs of Toffoli gates by introducing approximations. While approximations introduce errors to the output of the Toffoli gate, they can reduce the depth and gate count of the implementation. This thesis finds that discrete errors in two-qubit and three-qubit controlled Toffoli gates have been utilized to reduce the gate counts in such a way that the implementation is exact cancelling the errors. Additionally, continuous errors are utilized to reduce the depth of a multi-controlled Toffoli gate decomposition in ancilla-free settings. However, this review also demonstrates other, non-approximate, construction of multi-controlled Toffoli gate, which achieves comparable implementation costs demonstrating marginal gains for the approximation techniques currently.

title: Limitations of evaluation metrics under class imbalance
abstract: Class imbalance is a common issue in machine learning-based classification tasks, where some classes are underrepresented in comparison to others. This thesis investigates the effect of class imbalance on the interpretation of commonly used evaluation metrics, such as accuracy, balanced accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the ROC curve. The results of this study indicate that 1) accuracy may be misleading in imbalanced datasets, as it is highly dominated by the majority class, 2) balanced accuracy provides a more robust evaluation but still has limitations in reflecting prediction reliability, and 3) precision, recall, and F1-score provide more informative evaluations of the positive class but are still influenced by the classification threshold. The study also explores the ROC curve, with its area under the curve (AUC) serving as a more effective metric, although its reliability is debated in imbalanced datasets. These findings enhance the understanding of improving classifier evaluation in imbalanced real-world applications, emphasizing that combining multiple metrics is essential for a comprehensive assessment of classifier performance.

title: Zwischen Sicherheit, Vertrauen und digitaler Demokratie - wie wir in Zukunft wählen werden
abstract: Wenn jemand weiß, wie komplex, spannend und gleichzeitig sensibel das Thema elektronische Wahlen ist, dann Tobias Hilt – Wissenschaftler in der Forschungsgruppe SECUSO am Karlsruher Institut für Technologie (KIT). In dieser Folge von „Nachgefragt – wissen, wie’s läuft“, dem Podcast der Gesamtkommunikation des KIT, spricht Moderatorin Gabi Zachmann mit ihm darüber, wie sichere Online-Wahlen funktionieren können, warum technische Verifizierbarkeit allein nicht reicht – und wieso am Ende der Mensch oft der entscheidende Faktor ist. Von „wie kann ich sicher sein, dass meine Online-Stimme wirklich zählt?“ über „kann man Wahlbetrug im digitalen Raum erkennen?“ bis hin zu „sind wir in Deutschland überhaupt bereit für Internet-Voting?“ – Tobias gibt verständliche Einblicke in die Welt der kryptographischen Wahlsysteme und zeigt, wie Forschung daran arbeitet, digitale Demokratie vertrauenswürdig und zugänglich zu gestalten. Eine Folge über High-Tech, Wahlgeheimnis und die Frage, wie wir die Demokratie ins 21. Jahrhundert bringen – ohne ihre Grundpfeiler zu gefährden.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND PRACTICAL APPLICATION OF A REGRESSION MODEL IN THE PYTHON PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE
abstract: This thesis demonstrates the process of developing a regression model in the Python programming language and applying it in practical problems. Regression analysis, as a statistical method, plays a crucial role in determining the relationship between variables. The work examines the theoretical foundations of the linear regression model, the stages of its creation using the Python programming environment, and the possibilities of applying it based on real data. Also, ways to increase the effectiveness of regression models using modern libraries have been analyzed.

title: ІНТЕЛЕКТУАЛЬНІ ПОМІЧНИКИ НА ОСНОВІ ЧАТ-БОТІВ
abstract: У статті розглянуто сучасні тенденції розвитку інтелектуальних помічників на основі чат-ботів, які стають важливим інструментом цифрової трансформації науки та освіти. Розглянуто специфіку інтелектуальних чат-ботів, які використовують для комунікації з користувачем зовнішні бази знань та механізми пояснень для згенерованих рекомендацій. Проаналізовано проблеми застосування чат-ботів у науковій діяльності та визначено такі проблеми, як ризик «галюцинацій», відсутність семантичної узгодженості, складність інтеграції з інституційними інформаційними системами та потреба у формалізованому представленні знань предметної області. Окрему увагу приділено використанню чат- ботів у післядипломній освіті, де вони сприяють навігації у нормативних документах, організації дослідницьких процесів та персоналізації навчальних матеріалів. Охарактеризовано основні архітектурні моделі чат-ботів та методи аналізу природномовних документів, що визначають їх функціональні можливості. Практична частина статті присвячена розробці інтелектуального помічника для інформаційної підтримки післядипломної освіти. Система розроблена на базі платформи Vertex AI Agent Builder та поєднує flow-based та playbook-based агентів для оптимізації ресурсів та забезпечення гнучкої взаємодії з користувачами. Показано архітектурні та функціональні особливості системи, інтеграцію з великими мовними моделями (зокрема Gemini), а також можливості масштабування на рівні всієї структури НАН України. Зроблено висновок, що інтелектуальні чат-боти, побудовані на основі семантичних моделей та гібридних архітектур, здатні забезпечити ефективну підтримку наукових досліджень і освітніх процесів, зменшити адміністративне навантаження та сприяти формуванню сучасної інформаційної інфраструктури.

Розглянуто специфіку інтелектуальних чат-ботів, які використовують для комунікації з користувачем зовнішні бази знань та механізми пояснень для згенерованих рекомендацій. Проаналізовано проблеми застосування чат-ботів у науковій діяльності та визначено такі проблеми, як ризик «галюцинацій», відсутність семантичної узгодженості, складність інтеграції з інституційними інформаційними системами та потреба у формалізованому представленні знань предметної області. Окрему увагу приділено використанню чат- ботів у післядипломній освіті, де вони сприяють навігації у нормативних документах, організації дослідницьких процесів та персоналізації навчальних матеріалів. Охарактеризовано основні архітектурні моделі чат-ботів та методи аналізу природномовних документів, що визначають їх функціональні можливості. Практична частина статті присвячена розробці інтелектуального помічника для інформаційної підтримки післядипломної освіти. Система розроблена на базі платформи Vertex AI Agent Builder та поєднує flow-based та playbook-based агентів для оптимізації ресурсів та забезпечення гнучкої взаємодії з користувачами. Показано архітектурні та функціональні особливості системи, інтеграцію з великими мовними моделями (зокрема Gemini), а також можливості масштабування на рівні всієї структури НАН України. Зроблено висновок, що інтелектуальні чат-боти, побудовані на основі семантичних моделей та гібридних архітектур, здатні забезпечити ефективну підтримку наукових досліджень і освітніх процесів, зменшити адміністративне навантаження та сприяти формуванню сучасної інформаційної інфраструктури.

title: Multimodal Interaction Design for Automated Agent-to-Agent Interaction: A Survey
abstract: Automated agent-to-agent (A2A) interaction is a core mechanism for enabling intelligent collaboration across applications and is reshaping interaction paradigms in software systems. Traditional application integration relies on predefined APIs and rigid protocols, which struggle to accommodate dynamic coordination requirements. This paper systematically reviews A2A automated interaction mechanisms based on multimodal interaction design, covering theoretical foundations, technical architectures, applications, and future trends. A four-layer A2A architecture—comprising perception, interpretation, planning, and execution layers—is synthesized from representative frameworks including PCA-Bench, AutoGen, AgentVerse, and A-HMAD. To better justify this synthesis, the paper explicitly maps the perception–cognition–action chain in PCA-Bench, the conversable role-and-tool composition in AutoGen, the collaborative expert-group organization in AgentVerse, and the adaptive heterogeneous debate process in A-HMAD to the proposed four layers. Reported case studies suggest that multimodal approaches can reduce interaction latency by up to 32% and increase task success rates by up to 41% compared with unimodal methods; however, these figures are treated as scenario-specific evidence rather than directly comparable results under a unified experimental setting, because the underlying tasks, baselines, and evaluation protocols differ across studies. Three key challenges are identified: scalability issues from computational overhead, security risks including privacy leakage and adversarial attacks, and heterogeneous integration problems from semantic interoperability gaps. Future directions are further specified by application scenario: lightweight models are most suitable for edge and real-time A2A systems, federated learning is most suitable for privacy-sensitive cross-organization collaboration, and protocol standardization is most suitable for open ecosystems requiring cross-platform interoperability. This review provides structured understanding of multimodal A2A interaction and design guidance for next-generation intelligent collaborative systems.
